```text
[ ] Test and harness code guarded by WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS alone also carries !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING if the target forces dev tests on
[ ] No hand-added CrowdySDK CoreRedirects in DefaultEngine.ini
[ ] No HasMetaData calls remain in shipped runtime code
```

## Gotchas

- The cook rebakes the registry automatically. The manual rebuild only guards against inspecting a stale snapshot while you are still in the editor.
- A Shipping-only build failure will not show up in a Development or PIE cook. If code compiles everywhere except Shipping, check whether `bForceCompileDevelopmentAutomationTests` keeps your test files in the build, then look for a `!UE_BUILD_SHIPPING` region reached through an include, not through the line you changed.
- CoreRedirects apply on load, not retroactively. A stale reference in an unopened asset waits until that asset is loaded and saved, or resaved in bulk, before it resolves to the new path.

## Related

- [Inspector and Registry](../studio/inspector-and-registry.md): the Registry page's Rebuild (Deep Scan) button.
- [Map Profile](../runtime/map-profile.md): what a profile is and what reads it.
- [Project Settings](../reference/project-settings.md): the full field list, and which fields Config Sync writes.
- [Testing Locally](./testing-locally.md): the dev-only loopback and trace surface, adjacent to what Shipping strips.
- [Troubleshooting](./troubleshooting.md): symptom to cause to fix, including a profile asset that did not load.

# Troubleshooting
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/guides/troubleshooting

# Troubleshooting

This page matches a symptom to its likely cause and its fix. Read the table first; each row links to a
section with the full fix and the trace CVar that confirms it.

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | Trace CVar |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Nothing replicates on a map](#nothing-replicates-at-all) | A `MapProfiles` row or `DefaultProfile` names an asset that did not load, or networking is off on the resolved profile | Fix the asset path the warning names, or tick Enable Networking | `crowdy.entity.trace` |
| [Actors do not appear at all](#rendering-backend-not-set) | The map profile's Backend Class was cleared | Assign a `UCrowdyRenderingBackend` subclass | `crowdy.entity.trace` |
| [Entities register but are never drawn](#entities-register-but-are-never-drawn) | Backend Config empty, or its Replication Policy Class unset (2.14.0 and earlier) | Set a Crowdy Actor Pool Backend Config with a policy class | `crowdy.entity.trace` |
| [Only some remote entities of a class appear](#only-some-remote-entities-of-a-class-appear) | The actor pool never grew past 8 per class (2.16.0 and earlier), or it is at `MaxPoolSizePerClass` | Update to 2.17.0; raise the cap if it warns | `crowdy.pool.trace` |
| [A player who just joined is invisible until they move](#a-player-who-just-joined-is-invisible-until-they-move) | A known server issue: the actor's first update is refused and later ones are not relayed to other players | Nothing on the client fixes it yet; moving recovers | `crowdy.net.trace` |
| [An RPC never runs on other clients](#events-are-not-received) | Missing entity component, unregistered entity, recipient/distance settings, or a registry gap | Work through the four sub-causes in order | `crowdy.rpc.trace` |
| [A remote entity shows as the wrong class](#a-remote-entity-cannot-be-targeted) | The entity's class was never loaded on this client | Add the class to Preloaded Entity Classes | `crowdy.entity.trace` |
| [A CrowdyState property does nothing on a crowd-rendered actor](#a-crowdystate-property-does-nothing-on-the-crowd) | Mass-rendered entities need their own field registration | See [Add your own crowd data](../mass/add-your-own-crowd-data.md) | n/a |
| [Client cannot connect, or connects on one machine and not another](#connection-fails-ipv4-versus-ipv6) | Address-family mismatch, or the realtime connection never came up | Match the family, check the UDP path | `crowdy.net.trace` |
| [Thousands of warnings a second, frame rate drops](#a-refused-connection-floods-the-log) | The realtime connection was refused or never came up; every send after that logs | Confirm the connection came up before chasing anything else | `crowdy.net.trace` |
| [Code will not compile against the SDK](#module-dependency-or-include-errors) | Missing module dependency or missing include | Add the module, include the header | n/a |

## Nothing replicates at all

A project that configures nothing runs on the SDK's shipped default map profile, so "no profile" is not
the nothing-configured state. The map is inactive when a `MapProfiles` row or the `DefaultProfile` points
at an asset that did not load, or when **Enable Networking** is off on the profile that resolved.

With no profile resolved for the current map, the entity subsystem, the auto replicator, and the actor
manager do nothing. You get one warning in the log and otherwise no errors, so replication just looks dead.

Fix:

1. Read the warning. It names the asset path a `MapProfiles` row or `DefaultProfile` points at and says it
   "did not load; check that the asset still exists and is packaged". Fix the path, or the cook, first.
2. Open Project Settings, Plugins, Crowdy SDK, Map Profiles, and confirm the row for this map (or
   `DefaultProfile`) points at a `UCrowdyMapProfile` asset that opens.
3. On that profile, confirm `bEnableNetworking` is true. Keep the other defaults: Actor Pool backend and
   the auto replicator on.
4. A map with no row and no `DefaultProfile` runs on the shipped default; if that map should be inactive,
   give it a profile of its own with **Enable Networking** off.

The profile is resolved by `UCrowdySDKDeveloperSettings::ResolveProfileForWorld`. If no profile resolves,
the SDK logs "map resolved no map profile, so the SDK is inactive on it: no entity registration" and stays
off for that map.

:::tip[If a new map replicates nothing, read the profile warning before anything else: it names the asset that failed.]
:::

## Rendering backend not set

Actors never appear, even though the map profile resolves and `crowdy.entity.trace` shows entities
registering. The map profile's Backend Class was cleared: it defaults to `UCrowdyActorPoolBackend`, so
this state only follows an edit.

The actor manager warns "BackendClass is not set in the map profile" the first time it needs one.

Fix: open the map profile asset and assign a `UCrowdyRenderingBackend` subclass in the Backend Class field.
The Actor Pool backend that ships with the SDK is the right default for most games.

## Entities register but are never drawn

Backend Class is set, `crowdy.entity.trace` shows remote entities registering, and nothing appears. On
2.14.0 and earlier the actor pool refuses to initialize when its config is incomplete, and logs one of two
warnings:

- "Backend Config is not set, but this backend needs a CrowdyActorPoolBackendConfig to know what to
  spawn", when the profile's Backend Config is empty.
- "Replication Policy Class is not set on '...', so nothing would read the state arriving for these
  entities", when the config exists but names no policy.

Fix: update to 2.15.0, where an empty config falls back to the built-in `UCrowdyTransformRepPolicy` and
this state no longer occurs. On an older plugin, set **Backend Config** on the map profile to a Crowdy
Actor Pool Backend Config asset and its **Replication Policy Class** to a `UCrowdyRepApplicationPolicy`
subclass; see [Rendering backends](../runtime/rendering-backends.md) and
[What's changed](./whats-changed.md).

## Only some remote entities of a class appear

Another client spawns twenty entities of one class and this client shows eight. On 2.16.0 and earlier the
actor pool held `DefaultPoolSizePerClass` actors (8) per class and never grew: every entity past that logged
`Pool exhausted for <class>` and was never drawn, and one whose spawn event had already made an actor lost
that actor too.

Fix: update to 2.17.0, where the pool grows on demand up to `MaxPoolSizePerClass` (256) and an entity it
cannot draw yet is retried instead of dropped. If the log says a pool "is at its cap", raise
`MaxPoolSizePerClass` on the map profile's Actor Pool Backend Config. `crowdy.pool.trace` logs each
activation, each growth step, and each entity waiting at the cap; see
[Rendering backends](../runtime/rendering-backends.md#configure-it).

## A player who just joined is invisible until they move

A player spawns and stands still, and the other players do not see them until they take a step; this can last
a minute or more. The client is sending correctly. The replication server refuses each actor's first update
with `UNAUTHORIZED` while it loads the player's permissions, which is expected and logged once as "The server
rejected a send: code 7 (Unauthorized) ... ACTOR_UPDATE_REQUEST". Every later update is accepted, but the server
does not relay that actor to the other players, nor theirs to it, until the actor moves. This is a server issue
and has been reported.

Confirm it with `crowdy.net.trace 1` on both clients: each client's log shows its own actor coming back to it
(`Received opcode 130 for actor <its own id>`) every few seconds, and no line for the other player's actor until
one of them moves. "Transport totals" should show no verification failures and no drops. Until the server is
fixed, the actor becomes visible to everyone as soon as it moves.

## Events are not received

An RPC event (`CrowdyEvent`) reaches the call site but never runs `Name_Implementation` on other clients.
Work through these causes in order.

### The receiving actor has no entity component

An event is aimed at the entity that its sender object belongs to, by NetID. The receiving actor must carry
a `UCrowdyEntityComponent`. If the actor is not an entity, there is no NetID to route to and the event is
dropped.

Fix: add the component in the actor constructor.

```cpp
CrowdyEntity = CreateDefaultSubobject<UCrowdyEntityComponent>(TEXT("CrowdyEntity"));
```

### The entity is not registered, or the dispatch drops it

A Dynamic entity needs to register before it can send or receive. Until it registers it has no NetID on the
network, and a call aimed at an unregistered entity logs "target is not a registered entity, event dropped"
from `DispatchGameEvent` and goes nowhere.

- If `bAutoRegister` is off, call `StartReplication()` yourself.
- Confirm registration from `GetNetID()`. A registered entity returns a valid id.

### The recipient does not include this client

Check the `CrowdyRecipient` on the receiver function. The recipient decides who runs the body:

- `SpatialMulticast` (default): spatial and decay-thinned. Remote clients only run the event if they are in
  range.
- `Multicast`: a named channel, any distance, no decay.
- `OwningClient`: only the entity's owner.
- `Host`: only the elected host.

If you used the default `SpatialMulticast` and the other client is out of range, the event is thinned away
on purpose. Raise `CrowdyDistance` (values run `None` to `Eight_Chunks`, default `Eight_Chunks`) or relax
`CrowdyDecay` (default `No_Decay`). Decay and distance apply only to `SpatialMulticast`.

If you need delivery at any distance, switch to `Multicast` with a `CrowdyChannel`, or use `OwningClient` or
`Host` for targeted delivery.

:::note[The owner of a SpatialMulticast event runs the body locally and announces to the others. The owner never runs its own `Name_Implementation` from the network: an event is not delivered back to its sender, even where a Dynamic entity's owner sees its own echoed proxy.]
:::

### The event was never registered, or the receiving function cannot be found

Two failures look the same as a dropped event but come from a cook or a rename, not from recipients or
range.

A `CrowdyEvent` that never made it into the baked registry logs "not registered; calls to it will be
dropped" and every call to it is silently a no-op. This is a cook-time gap: cooked builds strip UObject
metadata, so the SDK reads `CrowdyEvent` markers from a baked registry built ahead of time, never from
`HasMetaData` at runtime. A function that shows up in the editor because the metadata is still there can be
missing from that registry in a packaged build, which is why the symptom can differ between a dev session
and a shipped build. Rebuild the registry before packaging if you added or renamed an event.

Separately, if the function itself cannot be found on the class, `ResolveFunction` logs "not found on class"
and the call is dropped. This is almost always a rename or a missing `UFUNCTION` on the `_Implementation`
function.

Turn on `crowdy.rpc.trace` to follow send, route, and recipient decisions for each event.

## A remote entity cannot be targeted

A client falls back to guessing a remote entity's type from its state struct, and gets it wrong when two
classes share one struct.

The receiver resolves an incoming entity update by a class id, and it only resolves that id among classes
already loaded in memory; it never loads a package to do so. A Blueprint entity class this client has never
spawned itself is not loaded, so the id cannot be named and its own declaration cannot be read. The same
gap makes the actor manager fall back to the state struct, which cannot tell two classes sharing one struct
apart.

`Preloaded Entity Classes` is empty by default in a new project. This is the default state, not an edge
case you are unlikely to hit.

Fix: Project Settings, Plugins, Crowdy SDK, Replication, Preloaded Entity Classes. Add every entity class a
client needs to display or target when it belongs to someone else.

:::note[Treat Preloaded Entity Classes as a deployment requirement, not a one-time test-rig setting.]
Any client that must display or target another client's entity needs that entity's class preloaded on this
client, whether or not this client ever spawns one itself.
:::

## A CrowdyState property does nothing on the crowd

A `CrowdyState` property that works perfectly on a normally-spawned actor does nothing when the same actor
is drawn as a crowd row by the Crowdy Mass Rendering Backend: the value is decoded and then silently dropped.

A normally-spawned actor needs nothing extra. An entity drawn as a crowd row needs its own field
registration before a `CrowdyState` property reaches it; see
[Add your own crowd data](../mass/add-your-own-crowd-data.md). For other crowd symptoms, such as a grey
crowd or no rows at all, see [Fix a crowd that does not look right](../mass/troubleshooting.md).

## Connection fails: IPv4 versus IPv6

If the client never connects, or connects on one machine but not another, the cause is often an
address-family mismatch between the client and the server endpoint: one side resolves to IPv6 and the
other only listens on IPv4, or the reverse.

Fix:

1. Check **UDP Protocol** under Project Settings, Plugins, Crowdy SDK. It is read-only there; set it on
   the Crowdy Studio Project page, Connection section. `Auto (IPv4)` and `Force IPv4` connect over IPv4,
   `Force IPv6` over IPv6, and neither falls back to the other family. On a network without working IPv6,
   `Force IPv6` is the mismatch. See [Connection and reconnect](../runtime/connection-and-reconnect.md).
2. Check that no local firewall is blocking the UDP path. The realtime plane runs over UDP; a blocked port
   looks like a silent connection failure.
3. Verify the app is configured for the correct backend (Dev, Production, or Custom) in Crowdy Studio, then
   run Config Sync so the URLs and the protocol in project settings match.

A UDP timeout during a live session is a different, self-healing case: the SDK logs "The UDP connection
failed, reconnecting" and retries on its own. It is not an error to act on unless the reconnect never
succeeds.

Turn on `crowdy.net.trace` to see connection attempts, the resolved endpoint, and the UDP handshake.

## A refused connection floods the log

Thousands of Warning lines a second, frame rate drops, and nothing else about the session looks unusual.

The realtime connection was refused or never came up, and every send attempt after that logs one Warning:
"the replication connection refused" a send, or "cannot open a replication connection without a game
instance" if it never had one to open.

:::caution[Count the Warning lines before you trust any other reading taken alongside them.]
A refused connection can produce thousands of Warning lines a second and cut your frame rate in half by
itself. If you are chasing a performance number or another symptom from the same run, a log with more than
a few hundred Warning lines in it is not a clean reading; the flood is the cause, not a side effect.
:::

Fix: confirm the connection actually came up. Look earlier in the log for a server assignment or a connect
failure, and fix that first before treating any other symptom recorded alongside the flood as real.

## Module dependency or include errors

Code does not compile after you call into the SDK, usually a missing module dependency or a missing
include.

The SDK is split across modules. Reference the right one for the API you call:

- `CrowdyReplication`: the entity subsystem (`UCrowdyEntitySubsystem`), the entity component, RPC events.
- `CrowdyServices`: high-level subsystems and statics: `UCrowdyUtilities`, `UCrowdyTeams`,
  `UCrowdyAvatars`, `UCrowdyChannels`, `UCrowdyHostSubsystem`.
- `CrowdySDK`: `UCrowdySDKSubsystem` (including voice).

Fix:

1. Add the module you need to your `Build.cs`.

```csharp
PublicDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[]
{
    "CrowdyReplication",
    "CrowdyServices",
    "CrowdySDK"
});
```

2. Include what you use. For RPC events, include the event header explicitly.

```cpp
#include "Replication/RPC/CrowdyEvent.h"
```

:::caution[Keep the module dependency graph acyclic. `CrowdyServices` depends on `CrowdyReplication`, which depends on `CrowdyNet`. Your module can depend on any of them; nothing of yours should be depended on by them.]
:::

## Still stuck

If a problem does not match anything above, turn on the relevant trace variable and read the log around
the failing action. See [Testing locally](./testing-locally.md) for the loopback CVars and how to reach a
symptom with one client, and [Log categories](../reference/log-categories.md) for the full set of
`LogCrowdy<X>` categories and their trace CVars.

A `LogHttp` `ConnectionError` burst against a backend host, with otherwise clean local connectivity, points
at your own network path, not the SDK. Check your route to the backend before filing a bug.

## Gotchas

- A map with nothing configured runs on the shipped default profile. The "resolved no map profile" warning
  means a configured profile asset did not load, and it is a warning, not an error.
- On 2.14.0 and earlier an empty Backend Config, or one without a Replication Policy Class, tracks entities
  and draws none; the warning names the field. 2.15.0 falls back to the built-in policy.
- Preloaded Entity Classes is empty by default. Add every entity class a client needs to see belonging to
  someone else, not just the ones it spawns itself.
- A `CrowdyState` property needs no setup on a normal actor, but needs its own field registration on a
  crowd-rendered one; see [Add your own crowd data](../mass/add-your-own-crowd-data.md).
- A refused connection can flood the log by itself; rule that out before trusting any other measurement
  from the same run.

## Related

- [Testing locally](./testing-locally.md): the loopback CVars for reproducing a symptom with one client.
- [Log categories](../reference/log-categories.md): every `LogCrowdy<X>` category and its trace CVar.
- [Fix a crowd that does not look right](../mass/troubleshooting.md): a grey crowd, missing rows, and the crowd diagnostics.
- [Add your own crowd data](../mass/add-your-own-crowd-data.md): field registration for crowd-rendered entities.

# Sample Project
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/guides/sample-project

# Sample Project

`crowdy-sdk-sample` is a small, real Unreal project that demonstrates the SDK feature by feature. Each feature is a switch you walk into: the switch fires, the feature runs, and you watch the result replicate across two Play in Editor clients.

:::note[This tour targets SDK 2.1.0, not the current SDK]
The plugin copy bundled in the repo is 2.1.0 (`Plugins/CrowdySDK/CrowdySDK.uplugin`), the release that introduced the current `GetCrowdyHasAuthority` name. It predates this site's own CrowdyState pages. The repo's README documents a few 2.1.0 additions, property replication on CrowdyState, replicated subsystems, host and ownership fields, as already present in the bundled plugin code, but none of the switches below exercise them, so this page does not either. For the current shapes, follow the Lantern in the [Quickstart](../quickstart.md).
:::

The code lives in the `CrowdySDKTest` module, under `Source/CrowdySDKTest/Public|Private/Sample`.

:::tip[Most examples ship as C++ and Blueprint side by side]
Read the C++ when you want the exact call site and types. Open the matching Blueprint under `Content/Interactions/` when you want to see the same wiring as nodes. Two examples, Persistence and Teams, are C++ only: there is no Blueprint counterpart for either in this repo.
:::

## The interact-switch pattern

The sample keeps feature code out of the player and the HUD. Each example is a trigger volume you overlap. This keeps every example self-contained and lets you trigger one feature at a time.

Two pieces drive it:

- `ISampleInteractable` is an interface with one method, `Interact(APawn*)`. Anything that reacts to the player implements it.
- `ASampleSwitchBase` is a trigger box. On overlap it calls `Interact` on itself, passing the overlapping pawn.

Each example subclasses `ASampleSwitchBase` and overrides `Interact`. Walk into the box, and that example's code runs with a reference to your pawn.

```cpp
void ASampleObjectSwitch::Interact(APawn* Instigator)
{
    // Each switch puts its one feature here.
    // The base class has already detected the overlap and handed you the pawn.
}
```

## Shared data

`SampleTypes.h` holds the structs the examples pass around:

- `FSampleEntityState` (Location, Rotation, Velocity, bIsFalling) is the snapshot a continuous-state executor sends on the wire.
- `FSampleSpawnInfo` (Tint, DisplayName) is the spawn `InitialState` for a new entity.
- `FSampleProgress` (Level, LastLocation), tagged `USTRUCT(meta=(CrowdyPersistent))`, is what the Persistence example saves and loads.
- `FSampleItem` (Id, Count) is a small struct declared to show an array-of-structs RPC parameter; nothing in the repo uses it yet, and it has no switch of its own.

## The examples

Eight switches, each demonstrating one part of the SDK.

| Example | Switch | SDK feature it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MimicMe | `ASampleMimicSwitch` | Dynamic entity with a continuous-state executor |
| Object spawn-move-rotate-destroy | `ASampleObjectSwitch` | Spawn and destroy, plus RPC events with direct parameters |
| Ghost | `ASampleGhostSwitch` | Owner tracking: your own state echoed back as a proxy |
| Voice | `ASampleVoiceSwitch` | Voice chat capture and playback |
| Channel announce | `ASampleChannelSwitch` | Multicast RPC over a self-provisioned channel |
| Host spawn | `ASampleHostSwitch` | Host authority gate |
| Persistence | `ASamplePersistenceSwitch` | Push and pull saved gameplay state |
| Teams | `ASampleTeamsSwitch` | Find or create a team, join it, leave it on the next interact |

### MimicMe

`ASampleMimicSwitch` spawns `ASampleMimicEntity`, an invisible puppeteer built around a `UCrowdyEntityComponent`. Each tick, the entity mirrors the interacting pawn's transform, computed by `UMathOperations::GetMimicTransform`, through the `ISampleMirrorSource` interface it implements (`GetMirrorTarget`, `GetMirrorPlaneTransform`). `USampleMimicExecutor` reads that mirror source and streams the result as an `FSampleEntityState`.

The same struct shape is the one the SDK's general-purpose transform executor expects. `USampleTransformExecutor`, a `UActorUpdateExecutor`, implements the two functions any continuous-state executor needs:

```cpp
FInstancedStruct USampleTransformExecutor::GetActorState_Implementation(const UActorComponent* UpdateComponent) const
{
    // Reads the owning actor's transform and packs it into an FSampleEntityState.
}

UScriptStruct* USampleTransformExecutor::GetStateStruct_Implementation() const
{
    return FSampleEntityState::StaticStruct();
}
```

The AutoReplicator polls the executor about ten times a second, only on the owner. Remote clients apply the snapshot through the rendering backend. See [Continuous State](../runtime/continuous-state.md).

:::tip[ProxyClass here is a split-puppeteer detail, not a general rule]
`ASampleMimicSwitch` exposes a `ProxyClass` (falling back to `MimicClass` when unset) because this example splits the invisible puppeteer from the visible proxy the other clients see. Most Actor Pool entities do not need to touch `ProxyClass` at all.
:::

:::warning[The replication policy base class is abstract]
`USampleTransformReplicationPolicy` subclasses `UCrowdyRepApplicationPolicy` (`ExtractFields`, `ApplyToActor`, `OnInstanceDeactivated`) to interpolate position and rotation and latch velocity and the falling flag. Without a concrete subclass registered on the entity's `ReplicationPolicyClass`, the backend init bails and replication silently no-ops. If MimicMe stops moving on remote clients, this is the first thing to check.
:::

### Object spawn-move-rotate-destroy

`ASampleObjectSwitch` cycles through four actions on `ASampleObjectEntity`, a Static-mode `UCrowdyEntityComponent` actor: spawn, move, rotate, destroy.

- Spawn and destroy go through the entity spawn API.
- Move and rotate are RPC events whose parameters arrive directly, with no payload struct.

```cpp
UFUNCTION(meta=(CrowdyEvent, CrowdyRecipient="SpatialMulticast"))
void SetObjectLocation_Implementation(FVector NewLocation);
CROWDY_EVENT(SetObjectLocation)

UFUNCTION(meta=(CrowdyEvent, CrowdyRecipient="SpatialMulticast"))
void SetObjectRotation_Implementation(FRotator NewRotation);
CROWDY_EVENT(SetObjectRotation)
```

Calling `SetObjectLocation(NewLocation)` runs the body on the owner and announces it to the others, who run `SetObjectLocation_Implementation`. See [Entities and Spawning](../runtime/entities-and-spawning.md) and [RPC Events](../runtime/rpc-events-cpp.md).

### Ghost

`ASampleGhostSwitch` toggles `UCrowdyActorTracker::ToggleOwnerTracking`. With owner tracking on, the server echoes your own state back to you, and the backend draws it as a proxy: a true network round trip of yourself, not a local copy.

:::caution[Your player pawn must be a Dynamic Crowdy entity for there to be any state to echo.]
:::

### Voice

`ASampleVoiceSwitch` toggles voice chat on `UCrowdySDKSubsystem`:

- `StartVoiceChat` and `StopVoiceChat` control the microphone.
- `PlayVoiceChat` and `MuteVoiceChat` control hearing others.

No wrapper is needed; the subsystem methods are BlueprintCallable.

```cpp
UCrowdySDKSubsystem* Voice = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UCrowdySDKSubsystem>();
Voice->StartVoiceChat();
```

See [Voice Chat](../services/voice-chat.md).

### Channel announce

`ASampleChannelSwitch` is a Static entity with a Stable identity policy. On interact it self-provisions its channel: it looks up `SampleWorldChat`, creates it with an Open policy if it does not exist yet, joins it, and registers for reliable RPC on it. `Announce`, its Multicast event, is then routed over that channel.

The event takes four parameters directly:

```cpp
UFUNCTION(meta=(CrowdyEvent, CrowdyRecipient="Multicast", CrowdyChannel="SampleWorldChat"))
void Announce_Implementation(const FString& InMessage, uint8 InMood, const TArray<int32>& InScores, TSubclassOf<AActor> InIcon);
CROWDY_EVENT(Announce)
```

A matching `BlueprintImplementableEvent OnAnnounceReceived` carries the same four parameters for a Blueprint listener. A Multicast event reaches channel members at any distance with no decay.

For raw channel sends and the membership cache, see [Channels](../runtime/channels.md).

### Host spawn

`ASampleHostSwitch` spawns a world object, but only when `UCrowdyUtilities::GetCrowdyHasAuthority(this)` returns true.

```cpp
if (UCrowdyUtilities::GetCrowdyHasAuthority(this))
{
    UCrowdyUtilities::SpawnCrowdyEntity(this, WorldObjectClass, SpawnTransform, FInstancedStruct());
}
```

:::note[The host is a convention, not an enforced server role, so this shows how to gate work to the one elected client.]
:::

See [Host Authority](../runtime/host-authority.md).

### Persistence

`ASamplePersistenceSwitch` pushes, then pulls, an `FSampleProgress` for the interacting player pawn.

```cpp
FSampleProgress Progress;
Progress.Level = 3;
Persistence->PushState<FSampleProgress>(Progress, PlayerActor);

Persistence->PullState<FSampleProgress>(PlayerActor,
    [](bool bSuccess, const FSampleProgress& Loaded)
    {
        // Runs on the game thread.
    });
```

:::note[Push goes over UDP and is fast. Pull goes over GraphQL and is async, and the callback runs on the game thread.]
:::

Persistence is being retired from the current SDK; see the Persistence section of [What's Changed](./whats-changed.md) for what replaces it and what stays working in the meantime.

### Teams

`ASampleTeamsSwitch` shows both sides of teams from gameplay code, through `GameInstance->GetSubsystem<UCrowdyTeams>()`. Its one authored property is `TeamName` (default "Sample Team"). Interacting looks the name up with `GetTeams`, joins the team if it exists and creates it (Open policy, the creator is added as a member) if not; interacting again leaves it. Membership is read from the cache with `IsPlayerInTeam` and corrected when `OnMyTeamsCacheChanged` fires.

```cpp
// Found by name in the GetTeams result: join it.
TeamsSub->JoinTeam(FoundId, OnJoined, OnError);

// Not found: create it; the current player becomes a member.
TeamsSub->CreateTeam(TeamName, TEXT("Created from the sample"),
    ECrowdyTeamMembershipPolicy::Open, OnCreated, OnError);
```

The 2.1.0 plugin still names these types `FCrowdyGroup` and reads `GroupId`; the current SDK calls them `FCrowdyTeam` and `TeamId` (see [What's Changed](./whats-changed.md)).

Read the cache for instant UI and treat the callbacks as eventual truth. See [Teams](../services/teams.md).

## Required setup

The sample project is already set up for you. Sign up for a developer account, then log in through Crowdy Studio and again through the game. Sync the app first if it is not already synced. Logging in through the game yields the identity session token; an app-scoped token for the app is minted from it before replication works. See [Authentication](../services/authentication.md).

## Gotchas

- This repo's `Plugins/CrowdySDK` has no `CrowdyCppBridge` or `CrowdyNodes` module folder. If you go looking for current-SDK modules here, you will not find them; they postdate this vendored copy.
- Eight examples exist in this repo, not nine. An earlier version of this page named a ninth, `ASampleChannelsSwitch`, that does not exist in `Source` or `Content`.
- Persistence and Teams have no Blueprint counterpart in `Content/Interactions/`, unlike the other six examples.
- `GetCrowdyHasAuthority` is already the current name in this sample; there is no rename to make here.
- If the transform replication policy has no concrete subclass registered on `ReplicationPolicyClass`, replication silently does nothing. There is no error to look for.

- [Testing Locally](./testing-locally.md) for the loopback and trace CVars this sample's own README testing steps use.
- [Entities and Spawning](../runtime/entities-and-spawning.md) for the entity component and the spawn API.

# What's Changed
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/guides/whats-changed

# What's Changed

The customer-visible changes to the Unreal SDK since 2.0 / 2.1, newest first, each with what changed and what your project does about it. The list comes from a diff of the 2.1.0 public headers against 2.15.0 plus what each release since carried; anything not listed here kept its name, its pins, and its behavior as far as that diff shows.

## When you come here

You built against the SDK in July, you are updating the plugin to 2.15 or later (2.21.2 is current), and you want the list of things that compile differently, behave differently, or no longer exist, before you open the editor. Read top to bottom once. The entries that can break a C++ build are the teams rename (between 2.1.0 and 2.12.0), the removed `DevLogin` (2026-08-30), in 2.15.0 the array delegates, in 2.19.0 the removal of the Game Model API (see [its entry](#2026-10-12-sdk-v2190)), and in 2.20.0 the renamed pin delegates of the Channels, Teams, Avatars and sign-in nodes, which a C++ `AddDynamic` handler binds to (see [On Error](#2026-10-16-sdk-v2200)). In 2.21.0, a C++ `AddDynamic` handler bound to the **Call Server Function** action's **On Success** or **On Failed** needs one more parameter, `FName Code` (see [its entry](#2026-10-26-sdk-v2210)).

:::caution[The Game Model entries below no longer reach a server, and the API is removed.]
The SDK's Game Model API (containers and attributes, Effects, sessions, pre-seeding) was built on the game API's legacy game-model engine, which ck-exec replaced; the game API no longer serves it. The entries that describe it are kept as history. Do not adopt it: v2.18.0, the release that adds Server Objects, deprecates it, and v2.19.0 removes it, as described under [2026-10-12 (SDK v2.19.0)](#2026-10-12-sdk-v2190). Its replacement is [Server Objects](../exec/overview.md), described under [2026-10-07 (SDK v2.18.0)](#2026-10-07-sdk-v2180); [Move from Game Models](../exec/move-from-game-models.md) says what to change.
:::

## 2026-10-29 (SDK v2.21.2)

- **Read kit actors without a copy.** The Crowdy Kit Actor subsystem gains **Get Kit Actor Count** (**Kind**) and **Get Kit Actor** (**Kind**, **Index**, **Kit Actor** out, returns a bool), and C++ `ViewKitActors(FName Kind)`, which returns a const reference. **Get Kit Actors** still works but copies everything. **Kind** None means every kind for the nodes; for `ViewKitActors` it is the actors of no named kind. **What you do:** a per-tick read, such as a Mass map's Blueprint, switches to Count and Get Kit Actor; follow an actor by its id, since its index changes as others come and go. See [Show a starter's actors](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#show-a-starters-actors).
- **Kit actors are placed by the session's chunk size.** They used a fixed 1600; they now use `UCrowdyGameSession::SetChunkSize`. `FCrowdyKitActorState` gains `ChunkPosition`, the raw chunks the hub sent, and `Location` stays in world units. **What you do:** nothing. See [Show a starter's actors](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#show-a-starters-actors).
- **A starter's On Changed runs once at Ready.** **On X Changed** and **On Variables Changed** no longer also run before Ready, so a snapshot pushed while Connecting does not announce. **What you do:** nothing, unless a graph relied on the early run. See [Follow a variable](../exec/from-blueprint/read-and-follow-variables.md#follow-a-variable).
- **Owner Values the object does not read report no value.** Inventory, Wallet and Progress of another player's `CSO_Kit_Player`, or of any while signed out, now give **Has Value** false, not an empty value with true. **What you do:** branch on **Has Value** where you showed an empty one. See [Values only the player reads](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#values-only-the-player-reads).
- **Owner Values are read again after a pushed hub restart.** **What you do:** nothing. See [Values only the player reads](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#values-only-the-player-reads).
- **A snapshot's value wins over an Owner Value of the same field.** In a customized starter whose snapshot carries a field that is also an Owner Value, the value used to freeze. **What you do:** nothing. See [Values only the player reads](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#values-only-the-player-reads).
- **No Get Server State where nothing is visible.** It is not offered for a Server Object whose State has no player-visible variables, such as `CSO_Kit_Npcs`; an existing node on one fails to compile with a message. **What you do:** remove the node. See [Get a variable](../exec/from-blueprint/read-and-follow-variables.md#get-a-variable).
- **Config ids that differ only by case are refused.** **Add starter** and **Deploy** refuse a starter Config with two ids of one kind (item, currency, faction, counter, pity group) that differ only by case, since the SDK reads them as one. **What you do:** rename one. See [Add a starter](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#add-a-starter).
- **Bad kit actor updates are dropped.** An update with a **Name** over 128 bytes or a **Mode** over 32 bytes is dropped, and so is one whose id, hp, max hp or owner is not a whole 64-bit integer. **What you do:** nothing. See [Show a starter's actors](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#show-a-starters-actors).
- **Call as Developer from the command line reaches a starter's read-only player functions.** `-op=call` calls them as the developer, today the npcs starter's `state`. **What you do:** nothing. See [Call a function as the developer](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#call-a-function-as-the-developer).
- **The director publishes less.** While an encounter runs it publishes only events on a hit or a build; the next tick, at most 500 ms later, carries the snapshot. The hit reply still returns health at once. **What you do:** nothing. See [Defend against waves](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#defend-against-waves).
- **The zone's realtime event carries `centerZ`.** The ZoneChange event gains `centerZ` beside `centerY`, the same ground value. **What you do:** nothing. See [Shrink a circle](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#shrink-a-circle).
- **A sign-in can be cancelled without signing out.** `CancelSignIn()` on the Crowdy Authentication subsystem (and on the Crowdy SDK Subsystem) stops a restore, a password sign-in, an email link or social sign-in waiting for the browser, or one held for the terms. Only the call's `OnError` answers, with `Sign-in cancelled.`, and a cancelled restore keeps the saved session, which `Logout` would delete. `IsSignInPending()` says when a Cancel button makes sense. **What you do:** if your sign-in screen's Cancel or Back button calls `Logout`, call `CancelSignIn` instead so a returning player keeps their saved session. See [Cancel a sign-in](../services/authentication.md#cancel-a-sign-in).

## 2026-10-28 (SDK v2.21.1)

- **Blueprint sign-in starts from the Game Mode, not the Game Instance's Event Init.** A Blueprint Game Instance's **Event Init** runs before the SDK's subsystems exist, so the earlier Blueprint examples, which signed in and bound events there, failed: **Login** and **Restore Session** reported "subsystem not found" and **Bind Event** bound nothing. The examples now run from the Game Mode's **Event BeginPlay** and check **Is Signed In** first, since BeginPlay runs again in every map. C++ examples, which use `Init` after `Super::Init()`, are unchanged. **What you do:** if your Blueprint Game Instance signs in or binds SDK events in Event Init, move that graph to your Game Mode's Event BeginPlay. See [Signing in](../services/authentication.md#signing-in).
- **Two packaged clients can sign in as different accounts.** Clients sharing a `Saved` folder (Development copies in one folder, or any Shipping copies of one Windows user) shared one saved session. Start each extra client with `-crowdysession=<name>`, and it keeps a session of its own; with no switch the default session is used, so existing sign-ins still restore. **What you do:** nothing, unless you run several clients from one folder. See [Two packaged or standalone clients](./testing-locally.md#two-packaged-or-standalone-clients).
- **A deploy leaves a dropped type's Server Objects to the platform.** The platform now stops the Server Objects of a type a deploy or a rollback drops, keeping their saved state, and drops that type's switch, so the SDK no longer restarts those types before it deploys. `-op=deploy`'s result loses `stoppedRemoved` and `stopRemovedFailed`, and `-op=instances` gains `orphaned`, true for a Server Object whose type the active version does not deploy. **What you do:** a script that reads `stoppedRemoved` or `stopRemovedFailed` stops reading them. See [From the command line](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#from-the-command-line).
- **CrowdyCPP 0.74.0.** The realtime library moves from 0.73.0 to 0.74.0, which reads `orphaned` on each Server Object; the SDK sends and receives as before. **What you do:** nothing.

## 2026-10-26 (SDK v2.21.0)

:::caution[Updating from 2.20.0: two things to do]
1. **Run Generate Server Code once on every Server Object type** (the **Generate** button on Server Compute does all of them). Generated crates now pin ckx-sdk 0.12.1, and Server Compute refuses to deploy a crate generated before; your `logic.rs` is kept.
2. **In C++, add an `FName Code` parameter to a handler bound with `AddDynamic` to the Call Server Function action's On Success or On Failed.** The delegate has a fifth parameter, so the build breaks until you do.
:::

### Game Kit starters

- **The Game Kit starters are Server Object types.** **Add starter** on Server Compute, or `-op=addstarter`, adds any of the platform's seventeen [Game Kit](/game-kit/intro) starters (`world`, `matchmaker`, `session`, `leaderboard`, `player`, `market`, `npcs`, six game modes, `deck`, `arena`, `race` and `ball`) to the project as an ordinary type, with the starters it needs: its Rust under `Server/<Type Name>/`, its definition `CSO_Kit_*` under `/Game/ServerObjects/GameKit/`, its values as C++ structs in `CrowdyGameKitTypes.h`. A game uses it with the nodes it already knows, and the definition's new **Game Kit** category holds what only starters have. With `world` added, `world` is the app's root and the **Game Kit World** setting points **Get Players Online** at it. `-op=removestarter` removes a starter and those that need it. **What you do:** nothing, unless you want a starter. See [Use the Game Kit starters](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md).
- **Refused, and a Code on every call's answer.** `ECrowdyServerCallOutcome` has a new last value, **Refused**, for a starter's refusal of the game's own, such as a full match, and `FCrowdyServerCallResult` a `Code` (`FName`), such as `full`; your own types never answer Refused. The **Call** nodes have an advanced **Code** pin, and the Call Server Function action's delegate `FCrowdyServerCallDone` has a fifth parameter, `FName Code`. **This breaks a C++ build** that binds On Success or On Failed with `AddDynamic`. **What you do:** add the parameter; give a Blueprint Switch on the outcome that lists every pin a **Refused** pin if it calls a starter. See [Refusals and their codes](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#refusals-and-their-codes).
- **Find Match, Is My Turn and Get Turn Player.** An async **Find Match** node joins a matchmaker queue, follows it and accepts the match; **Is My Turn** and **Get Turn Player** read a session's turn. In C++, `CrowdyKit::FindMatch` and its siblings in `CrowdyGameKitMatch.h`. **What you do:** nothing. See [Find a match and take turns](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#find-a-match-and-take-turns).
- **A starter's actors are drawn as classes you choose.** A starter whose server code moves actors, such as the mobs of `npcs` or the ball, has them drawn as the classes its **Kit Actors** names, each with a **Crowdy Kit Actor** component holding its **Kit Actor** (with the **Instance Id** of the hub to call for it); the new **Game Kit Actor Starters** setting cooks them, and **Kit Actor Timeout** in the map profile ends one that stops updating. **What you do:** nothing. See [Show a starter's actors](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#show-a-starters-actors).
- **The Crowdy Server Object component reports where the player is.** For a starter with a **Position Function** (the arena, race and ball), the component sends the owner's place by itself, on real time so a paused game keeps reporting; new settings **Position Report** and **Snap To Kept Position**, and the event **On Position Kept**. **What you do:** nothing. See [Report where the player is](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#report-where-the-player-is).
- **Grant and deposit soft currency from Studio and the command line.** The `player` starter's row on Server Compute has **Grant soft currency...** and **Deposit soft currency...**, and the command line `-op=grant` and `-op=deposit`; **Call as Developer** and `-op=call` fill a starter function's empty `Ref` with a fresh one. Soft currency is game state, never real money. **What you do:** nothing. See [Grant and deposit soft currency from Studio](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#grant-and-deposit-soft-currency-from-studio).

### Parties, chat, emotes and spectating

- **Parties, guilds, chat rooms, emotes and spectating, as the Game Kit's other clients do them.** The **Crowdy Kit Social** subsystem and its nodes make parties, guilds and chat rooms on teams and channels, with **Send Chat** and **On Chat Message**; **Send Emote** and **On Emote** on **Crowdy Kit Emotes** reach the players nearby, within two budgets (`crowdy.kit.emotes.*` console variables); the **Crowdy Spectator** component keeps a player with no avatar receiving what happens near it. A client on 2.20.0 or older logs a Warning for each emote and spectator beat it hears. A CrowdyEvent whose generated type id would be 101, which the Game Kit's emote uses, takes another and logs a Warning naming both. **What you do:** nothing; if that Warning names one of your events, players on this SDK and on an older one stop exchanging it until they all update. See [Play together](../services/play-together.md).

### Deploying and Server Compute

- **A deploy builds in parts, reuses unchanged code, and stops the types it removes.** A project over 16 crates or 2 MB of source is built in parts instead of refused (staging versions with stand-ins named `ck_staged_`, a reserved prefix); a crate whose files match a revision the app holds is not built again (**Rebuild All and Deploy** and `-rebuild` build everything); and the running Server Objects of a type the deploy leaves out are stopped just before it. `-op=deploy`'s result gains `builds`, `reused`, `stagedVersions`, `restoredVersion`, `artifacts`, `stoppedRemoved` and `stopRemovedFailed`, and its top-level `buildId`, `buildStatus`, `buildLog` and `sdkVersion` describe the last build only and are absent when nothing was built. **What you do:** rename a type whose Type Name starts with `ck_staged_`; a script that reads `buildStatus` reads `ok` and `builds` instead. See [A deploy in parts](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#a-deploy-in-parts) and [The deploy's result](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#the-deploys-result).
- **Server Object crates pin ckx-sdk 0.12.1.** Generate writes `ckx-sdk = "0.12.1"` in a crate's `Cargo.toml` (it was `0.7.0`), and Deploy refuses a crate generated before. A **Generate** button on Server Compute, and `-op=generate`, generate every type that is out of date. **What you do:** press **Generate** once after updating; it keeps your `logic.rs`. See [Generate it](../exec/write-server-logic.md#generate-it).
- **A starter's variables have their Get and On Changed nodes.** On a starter's definition the menu offered no **Get** or **On Changed** for its variables, and a pasted one failed to compile; they work now, and a flag such as `bHasWave` has a **Get** and no **On Changed**, since **On Wave Changed** reports it. **What you do:** nothing. See [Read a value that may be none](../exec/use-game-kit-starters.md#read-a-value-that-may-be-none).
- **A type the active version lacks says it is not deployed**, as a type never deployed does, after you make an older version active; and a call while the connection redials into a paused or switched-off app reports **Paused** where it reported Timeout, as do the platform's new pause statuses. **What you do:** nothing. See [Outcomes](../exec/troubleshooting.md#outcomes).

### The command line and agents

- **Drive the editor, Server Compute and Crowdy Studio from a shell.** The Server Compute commandlet gains `whoami`, `generate`, `exporttype`, `newtype`, `edittype`, `removetype`, `renametype`, `addstarter`, `removestarter`, `grant`, `deposit`, `restart` without a type, `enable` for the whole app, more of `logs` and `stats`, and `batch` (several operations in one editor start); the new `-run=CrowdyStudio` commandlet syncs, creates apps and manages access features, teams, channels and grids. Operations that write the project refuse while any Unreal Editor is running unless you pass `-editoropen`, and those that change the Game Kit settings refuse a read-only `DefaultGame.ini`. **What you do:** nothing; point a coding agent at [For AI agents](../for-ai-agents.md#drive-the-editor-without-a-window). See [From the command line](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#from-the-command-line) and [Sync from the command line](../studio/config-sync.md#sync-from-the-command-line).

### Sign-in

- **On Login fires for every failed restore.** **On Login** now fires with `bSuccess` false for every failed session restore, `No saved session found` on a first launch included. **What you do:** if your false branch shows an error, skip that message, or call **Restore Session** only when **Has Saved Session** is true. See [Restore a saved session](../services/authentication.md#restore-a-saved-session).
- **A sign-in under way is cancelled by a logout or Clear Saved Session.** A sign-in, token mint, refresh or link still in flight then reports `Signed out before sign-in finished.` on the caller's **On Error** and signs nobody in. **What you do:** call **Clear Saved Session** only when no sign-in is under way. See [Session persistence and sign-out](../services/authentication.md#session-persistence-and-sign-out).
- **Other sign-in changes.** A sign-in held for consent fails at once in a process with no window instead of waiting forever; password sign-in and the app token are retried when the platform is busy (`crowdy.net.retry.busy`); a token answer with no runtime gate clears a pause; Server Objects reconnect when another account signs in; Development builds have `crowdy.auth.signin.file`, `crowdy.auth.status` and `crowdy.auth.signout`. **What you do:** nothing. See [Authentication](../services/authentication.md) and [Sign in from the console](../guides/testing-locally.md#sign-in-from-the-console).

### Crowdy Studio

- **Studio fixes.** A team role offers the team permissions (Manage Team, Manage Members, Manage Roles, Invite Members) and no longer Send Messages; a maximum set back to unlimited shows unlimited; an organization-token sign-in survives a network error; the module loads in the Default phase. **What you do:** nothing. See [Teams and channels](../studio/teams-and-channels.md).

### Runtime and Mass

- **The actor tracker's Configure applies only before the tracker starts**, which is before any Blueprint can call it, so it now logs a Warning and changes nothing; the node is deprecated. **What you do:** set the limits in the map profile or the developer settings and remove the call, Blueprint or C++, or the actors past the profile's limit stop being tracked. See [The actor tracker](../runtime/entities-and-spawning.md#the-actor-tracker).
- **An actor id that is not hexadecimal keys apart.** **To Guid** now hashes such an id instead of reading it as `FFFFFFFF` parts. **What you do:** derive again a key you saved from such an id.
- **A promoted shell is hittable only on its character mesh** and on components tagged `CrowdyTraceCollision`, and a Mass trace the grid cannot handle tests every entity. **What you do:** tag a hand-made hit box `CrowdyTraceCollision`. See [The near tier component's settings](../mass/promote-close-entities-to-actors.md#the-near-tier-components-settings).
- **Smaller changes.** A **Watch Record** added from a records handler runs once; the typed **Call** node labels its limit pin **Call Timeout** when the function has a **Timeout** input; an **Allowed Exec Gateway Domains** entry that is not a domain is named in a Warning; `crowdy.registry.dump` logs the baked registry; **Sync Actions Into Bank** can be called from a script. **What you do:** correct a gateway domain entry the Warning names; nothing else.

### CrowdyCPP 0.73.0

- **CrowdyCPP 0.73.0, and On Send Refused.** The realtime library moves from 0.67.0 to 0.73.0; the SDK sends and receives as before. The platform has two access tier permissions for realtime messages, `use_text_chat` and `use_direct_messages`, and the new **On Send Refused** event (`UCrowdyCppReplicationSubsystem::OnSendRefused`) reports each send the server refused and the permission it needs. **What you do:** nothing; bind On Send Refused if the player should hear that a chat or an event went nowhere. See [When the server refuses a send](../runtime/connection-and-reconnect.md#when-the-server-refuses-a-send).

## 2026-10-16 (SDK v2.20.0)

:::caution[After updating, generate the server code of every type with a timer or a player event before you deploy.]
The generated code changed for types with a timer, **On Player Joined**, **On Player Left** or **Remove Members Who Leave**. Until you run **Generate Server Code** on each of them, Server Compute marks it **Out of date** and refuses to deploy the project, and so does `-op=deploy`. Your `logic.rs` is kept. If CI deploys, commit the regenerated `Server/` folder.
:::

- **A Server Object type can ask for more platform data.** A new **Platform Data** category in the definition holds **Reads World Data**, moved there from **Access**, and eight new settings: **Reads Players**, **Changes Players' App State**, **Changes the World**, **Reads Grids**, **Manages Grids**, **Grants Grid Permissions**, **Reads Players' Access** and **Manages Players' Access** (`bReadsPlayers`, `bWritesPlayerState`, `bWritesWorld`, `bReadsGrids`, `bManagesGrids`, `bGrantsGridPermissions`, `bReadsAccess`, `bManagesAccess`). Deploy asks the platform for a permission for each one ticked, so the server code can read players, change a player's app state, write voxels, read or manage grids, grant grid permissions, or read and manage players' access to the app. Before, Deploy could ask only for `players.read` and `world.read`, and the platform refused the others. **What you do:** tick what your server code uses, and deploy. See [Platform data](../exec/access-members-and-timers.md#platform-data).
- **Deploy warns about platform data the code uses without asking for it.** Before it sends anything, the Deploy dialog lists each call into platform data whose setting is off, and `-op=changes` and `-op=deploy` add them as `warnings`. They do not stop a deploy. See [Deploy](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#deploy).
- **A changed Platform Data setting is a change to deploy.** Before, ticking **Reads World Data** alone left the type at **No changes** with **Deploy** unavailable. The **Changed** badge now also lists platform data and player access.
- **A type players cannot reach is closed to them.** A type whose functions are all **Server Only**, with no variable **Visible to Players**, no records, no members and neither player event, is now deployed with players kept out of it, and Server Compute says "closed to players". Acquiring one in a game is refused at once with a reason saying so; before, it failed after its first read. **What you do:** nothing; a game had nothing to read or call on such a type. Its next deploy lists it as changed (player access). See [A type players cannot reach](../exec/access-members-and-timers.md#a-type-players-cannot-reach).
- **A refusal by the platform says why.** A call the platform refused used to read "This player may not call Feed on this Server Object". It now reads "The server refused the call to Feed: " followed by the platform's own words. A call refused because its type or app is switched off or paused is a different outcome, **Paused**; see the entry below. A call the platform could not place, for example with the app at its instance limit, adds the platform's words after "The server could not be reached". A Server Object waiting to be read gives the same reasons, and one that could not connect at all now says why, such as a paused app, instead of a word like "Rejected". Refusals by your server code's own rules (**Callable By**, **Owner Only**, **Cooldown**) read as before, and every `Outcome` and `bRetryable` is unchanged except for Paused. **What you do:** if your game compares `Reason` with the old text, compare `Outcome` instead. See [Outcomes](../exec/troubleshooting.md#outcomes).
- **A Server Object type can set its own server limits.** A collapsed **Server Limits** category in the definition holds **Memory per Instance**, **Time per Call**, **Fuel per Call (Millions)** and **Calls Waiting** (`MemoryMegabytes`, `CallTimeLimitMs`, `FuelPerCallMillions`, `MaxWaitingCalls`). Before, every type ran with the platform's defaults: 64 MB, 2 seconds and 50 million fuel a call, and 1,024 waiting calls. Deploy sends only the ones you change, so a type that keeps them deploys as before, and a changed one is a change to deploy (the **Changed** badge lists server limits). A player's connection now waits up to 20 seconds for a call's answer instead of 10: the longest **Time per Call** plus time spent waiting behind other calls. **What you do:** nothing, unless a type needs longer calls, more memory, or less memory so more of them fit. See [Every setting](../exec/create-a-type.md#every-setting).
- **Server Compute can restart a type, and shows what runs.** A running type has a **Restart** button beside its switch: its running Server Objects are saved, stopped and started again on the live version at their next call, without refusing any calls, and players watching one read it again. After a deploy that changed a type with Server Objects still running the previous version, the Deploy card offers **Move now** or **Leave them**. Each type's line adds how many of its Server Objects are running, a red line names any the platform will not place and why, the header shows the app's Server Objects and reserved memory against its limits ("3 of 16 Server Objects · 192 of 1,024 MB"), and the **Budget paused** badge gives the platform's reason. The command line adds `-op=restart -type=T -yes` and `-op=instances`; `-op=status` gives the counts and limits, and a deploy's result its `sdkVersion`, the `ckx-sdk` the platform compiled against. Before, the only way to move running Server Objects to a new deploy was to switch the type off and on, which refused calls meanwhile. This needs a platform with ck-exec 0.15 or later. **What you do:** nothing. See [Restarting a type](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#restarting-a-type).
- **Call a Server Only function by hand, and Developers Only.** A Server Only function's Details now has **Call as Developer...**, which calls it on a live Server Object as you, the app's developer, with its inputs and the answer shown; the command line adds `-op=call -type=T -fn=F -key=K -inputs=<json> -yes`. **Callable By** gains **Developers Only**, for a function only a person should run: players and other server code are refused with "only developer tools may call this function". Before, a Server Only function could only be reached from other server code or a tool of your own. **What you do:** nothing; regenerate a type's server code after choosing Developers Only. See [Call a function as the developer](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#call-a-function-as-the-developer).
- **Get Players Online.** A new node, **Get Players Online** (`UCrowdyServerObjectLibrary::GetPlayersOnline`), gives how many players are in the app's world: the number the platform's realtime servers report, in which a player who leaves is still counted for a few minutes. The count is kept by the app's root Server Object, which Deploy now generates from `CSO_PlayersOnline` in the SDK's content and opens to players; before, the root kept nothing and players could not reach it. `CSO_PlayersOnline` works with every node that takes a definition, so **On Changed** follows the count. **What you do:** deploy once after updating the SDK: Server Compute offers a deploy until the app runs the new root, and until then **Get Players Online** returns false and logs why once. See [How many players are online](../exec/from-blueprint/read-and-follow-variables.md#how-many-players-are-online).
- **A project with no Server Object types can deploy, and the SDK's root is tracked.** Deploy used to need at least one type, and a removed last type kept running. It now sends the Crowdy SDK's own root alone, which keeps Players Online and removes every type; the confirm says "This project has no Server Object types, so only the Crowdy SDK's root (Players Online) is deployed." When a deploy removes types, the confirm adds "Their saved state is kept and is used again if you deploy them again." The root is also compared like a type: once a deploy from this SDK has recorded it, a later SDK whose root code differs makes Server Compute offer a deploy (the root is not a row), and an app whose root an earlier SDK deployed is compared only after your next deploy. **What you do:** deploy when Server Compute offers it. See [Deploy](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#deploy).
- **Generate is stricter about `root`, `lib.rs` and macros.** Generate refuses the SDK's own root definition ("This is the Crowdy SDK's own root; its server code is built into every deploy, so there is nothing to generate.") and a project type named `root`, and tells you to choose another Type Name. It asks before rewriting a `lib.rs` that loads a module file of your own (a top-level `mod name;` other than `logic` and `types`), with **No** as the default. When the `impl` block in `logic.rs` uses a macro such as `my_macro!(...)`, Generate and the Server Code tab no longer insert stubs, since the macro may define some functions; they copy them (**Copy Stubs**) instead. The question that offers stubs now says it writes into the file on disk and to save or close the file in another program first, and the tab says when another program saved the file without the functions Generate added. **Out of date** now names the first line that differs. **What you do:** declare your own modules at the top of `logic.rs` (`mod helpers;` there loads `src/logic/helpers.rs`), never in `lib.rs`. See [The Server Code tab](../exec/write-server-logic.md#the-server-code-tab).
- **Platform data hints are quieter and clearer.** The warning for a call into platform data the type did not ask for now ignores code in Rust raw strings and in `#[cfg(test)]` items. **Reads Players** shows ticked and greyed, with a tooltip naming why, when **Members From** is **Crowdy Team**, the records belong to Crowdy Teams, or a function players may call has a **Required Feature**; a Required Feature on a Developers Only or Server Only function no longer asks for `players.read`. **What you do:** nothing. See [Platform data](../exec/access-members-and-timers.md#platform-data).
- **A Cooldown or Required Feature on a function players cannot call is flagged.** A **Developers Only** or **Server Only** function with either shows a warning under it, and Deploy lists it ("... Cooldown has no effect, since only players' calls are limited." or "... Required Feature has no effect, since only players are checked."), because only players are limited and checked. **What you do:** clear the setting, or let players call the function. See [Required Feature](../exec/access-members-and-timers.md#required-feature).
- **Call as Developer reaches built-in functions, and big ids need quotes.** A built-in member function such as **Add Member** (when **Members From** is **This Object**) has a play button on its row in the Members list, and `-op=call -fn=` finds functions by name, built-ins included. In the command line's JSON inputs, a 64-bit integer above 9007199254740991 must be a string, for example `"Player": "9007199254740993"`; a larger unquoted number is refused. **What you do:** quote such ids in `-inputs`. See [Call a function as the developer](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#call-a-function-as-the-developer).
- **Server Compute compares limits the way the platform applies them.** A limit that is out of range counts as the nearest value in range, and a limit written as a string is read as a number, so another tool's manifest no longer shows "server limits" as changed forever. After a deploy, the offer to move running Server Objects decides which ran the previous version from the Server Objects read as the deploy was sent (by their epoch), not from your computer's clock. **What you do:** nothing. See [Overview](../exec/deploy-with-server-compute.md#overview).
- **A call past its Time per Call restarts the Server Object.** The platform answers the call `DeadlineExceeded` (the SDK reports **Timeout**, see the entry below for the reasons) and restarts that Server Object from its last save, so changes since the last save are lost. The limit covers the function itself, not the time a call waits behind others. **What you do:** keep functions short, and set **Save Every** low on a type whose recent changes matter. See [Server Limits](../exec/create-a-type.md#every-setting).
- **Get Players Online waits once a minute when the app has no root.** If the app has no Crowdy SDK root (deployed with an older SDK, or never deployed from Server Compute), the root now asks again once a minute, with the reason in the log, instead of every few seconds; once the app is deployed from Server Compute the count arrives without restarting the game. **What you do:** nothing. See [How many players are online](../exec/from-blueprint/read-and-follow-variables.md#how-many-players-are-online).
- **Retries are spread out.** Every Server Object retry and redial wait is now stretched by a random amount, up to half again: a failed read's first retry waits 1 to 1.5 seconds instead of exactly 1, a redial 1 to 1.5 seconds, then 2 to 3, up to 30 to 45, and a busy call's retries 0.25 to 0.375 seconds, then 0.5 to 0.75. Many players no longer retry in step after a server restart. **What you do:** nothing. See [Waiting is not failing](../exec/troubleshooting.md#waiting-is-not-failing).
- **A timeout says which side gave up.** The outcome is still **Timeout**, and `Reason` now tells the two apart. "AttackBoss ran past its Time per Call on the server: handler exceeded its deadline" means the server's own limit stopped the call (for a read, "The server took longer than this type's Time per Call to read this Server Object", or "watch"). "The server sent no answer in time; the connection may be slow or lost" means no answer reached the game within 20 seconds. **What you do:** nothing; show `Reason` as before. See [Outcomes](../exec/troubleshooting.md#outcomes).
- **A call to a switched-off or paused server comes back Paused.** `ECrowdyServerCallOutcome` has a new last value, **Paused**: the game's server, or the type, is switched off or paused (by its owner, or because the app ran out of funds). Calls refused this way used to come back **Denied**; they now come back **Paused** with `bRetryable` true and a reason such as "The server is switched off or paused, so it refused the call to Feed: `village_beacon` is switched off in app 123". A read or watch of such a server keeps trying, and its waiting reason reads "The server is switched off or paused, so this Server Object waits: " followed by the platform's words; a connection refused this way reads "The server is switched off or paused for `<Type Name>`: " followed by the error. **What you do:** a Blueprint Switch on the outcome gains a **Paused** pin to wire, and code that only checked for Denied should handle Paused too. See [Outcomes](../exec/troubleshooting.md#outcomes).
- **The Game Session tells you the app is paused.** `UCrowdyGameSession` (category **Crowdy SDK, Game Session**) has **Is App Paused** and **Get App Paused Reason**, both pure, and the event **On App Paused Changed** (`Paused`, `Reason`). It turns on when signing in or refreshing the app token reports the app paused, or when the realtime server refuses the player's updates because the app is paused, and off when a later token answer says the app is active, when the realtime server relays to the player again (or their updates go through for 15 seconds), and on sign-out. The realtime log line for that refusal now names the code `AppPaused`. **What you do:** show a "the world is paused" message instead of retrying. See [When the app is paused](../services/authentication.md#when-the-app-is-paused).
- **The Game Session tells you the player's access ended, and Server Objects stop.** `UCrowdyGameSession` has the event **On Access Ended** (`OnAccessEnded`: `Reason`, `BlockedUntil`) and the pure **Has Access Ended**, **Get Access Ended Reason** and **Get Access Blocked Until**. It fires when the player's access to the app ends: suspended, revoked, expired, signed out by the platform, or the account blocked. Every Server Object then fails with `Your access ended: ` followed by the reason, a call in flight or made later finishes with the new outcome **Access Ended** (`ECrowdyServerCallOutcome::AccessEnded`, not retryable), and nothing reconnects. A successful sign-in clears it; a **Crowdy Server Object** component and a typed node set to **Find By Asset** get their object again on their own, and code that calls `Acquire` itself calls it again. When the end time of a timed block is learned after access already ended, the event fires once more with it. **What you do:** show the reason and **Blocked Until**, return the player to the sign-in screen, and give a Blueprint Switch on the call outcome an **Access Ended** pin. See [When the player's access ends](../services/authentication.md#when-the-players-access-ends) and [Outcomes](../exec/troubleshooting.md#outcomes).
- **A revoked, suspended or missing access is told so too.** When a sign-in or the background token renewal is refused with `ACCESS_REVOKED`, `ACCESS_SUSPENDED` or `ACCESS_NOT_GRANTED`, **On Access Ended** fires with the server's message and **Blocked Until** carries a suspension's end, then the SDK stops renewing the token until the next sign-in. Before, only the Server Object connection's close and a blocked account ended access, so a game with no Server Object saw nothing. The realtime connection now also asks for a new app token when its reconnect is refused for an invalid token, so a sanctioned player hears it within seconds and a player whose access was restored reconnects, where before the reconnect failed until the game restarted. **What you do:** nothing beyond handling **On Access Ended**. See [When the app refuses the player's access](../services/authentication.md#when-the-app-refuses-the-players-access).
- **A blocked account is told so at sign-in.** Sign-in, register, the magic link, a social sign-in and a restored session fail with the server's message when the account is blocked, **On Access Ended** fires with **Blocked Until** (an ISO-8601 time, empty when the block lasts until it is lifted), and the app token is no longer rotated in the background until the player signs in again. **What you do:** show the message your sign-in screen already receives. See [When the account is blocked](../services/authentication.md#when-the-account-is-blocked).
- **Ban and unban a channel or team member.** New nodes **Ban Channel Member**, **Unban Channel Member**, **Ban Team Member** and **Unban Team Member**, and the C++ calls `BanChannelMember`, `UnbanChannelMember` on `UCrowdyChannels` and `BanTeamMember`, `UnbanTeamMember` on `UCrowdyTeams`. A ban takes an optional `Reason` of at most 500 characters (a longer one fails at once with a `PolicyViolation` error) and answers the member record with status `banned`; an unban answers `Was Banned`. A banned user's join, request to join or add fails with the new error code `Banned` in `ECrowdyChannelErrorCode` and `ECrowdyTeamErrorCode`, taken from the server's own code. **What you do:** nothing for existing code; a `switch` on the error code that lists every value needs a `Banned` case. See [Ban a member](../runtime/channels.md#ban-a-member) for channels and [Ban a member](../services/teams.md#ban-a-member) for teams.
- **On Error shows the error on Channels, Teams, Avatars and sign-in nodes.** The latent nodes' **On Success** and **On Error** now share one set of data pins: the result, then `Error` (with its `Code`) and `Message`; the sign-in nodes (**Login**, **Register**, **Restore Session**, **Begin Magic Link Sign In**, **Begin Social Sign In**) carry `Result` and `Message`, and **Record Player Consents** carries `Message`. Before, Blueprint could not read the error on **On Error**. On **On Success**, `Error` and `Message` are empty; on **On Error** the result is empty. A graph linked to the old pins keeps its links. In C++ the multicast pin types are renamed (`FChannelAsyncResult`, `FTeamAsyncResult`, `FAvatarAsyncResult` and the rest of that family, replacing the `...AsyncOnSuccess` ones, and `FAuthAsyncResult`, `FRecordPlayerConsentsAsyncResult` for sign-in); a C++ handler bound with `AddDynamic` to one of these pins takes the added parameters. The per-call `FOnChannel...`, `FOnTeam...` and `FOnAvatar...` delegates are unchanged. **What you do:** wire `Error` or `Message` where a graph needs the failure. See the nodes on [Channels](../runtime/channels.md#the-full-surface), [Teams](../services/teams.md#blueprint-nodes) and [Avatars](../services/avatars.md#async-action-nodes).
- **A Server Object gateway must be on the Game API's own domains.** The SDK now checks that the gateway the Game API names is on the Game API's own domains, as the C++ library's own connect does. A new Project Settings entry, **Crowdy SDK, Server Objects, Allowed Exec Gateway Domains** (`AllowedExecGatewayDomains`), lists extra domains for a server you host yourself. A gateway outside both is refused for good: every Server Object fails with "Could not open the connection to the server: the Game API named a gateway outside its own domains (...); if you host the server yourself, add its domain to Allowed Exec Gateway Domains in Project Settings", and it is not retried until you acquire an object again. **What you do:** nothing on the platform's servers; add your domain if you host the server yourself. See [Server Object gateway domains](../reference/project-settings.md#server-object-gateway-domains).
- **Players who left while a Server Object was stopped are cleaned up.** When a Server Object restarts, the platform does not tell it about players whose connection closed while it was stopped. The generated code now keeps the connection counts it restored as unconfirmed: right after the restart it tells watching players to read again, and any call from a player confirms them. A player not heard from within two minutes is treated as having left (**Remove Members Who Leave** removes them, `on_player_left` runs); a player who reconnects in that time just continues, and `on_player_joined` does not run again. The timer name `crowdy_sessions` is now reserved, and a definition with a timer of that name is refused. **What you do:** run **Generate Server Code** on each type with **On Player Joined**, **On Player Left** or **Remove Members Who Leave**, then deploy; until you do, Server Compute marks it **Out of date** and refuses to deploy the project. Rename a timer called `CrowdySessions`. See [Players who left while it was stopped](../exec/access-members-and-timers.md#players-who-left-while-it-was-stopped).
- **A changed timer keeps its old schedule if arming fails.** When a deploy changes a timer's **Runs**, running Server Objects arm the new schedule without stopping the timer first, so if arming fails the timer keeps its old schedule and the server log says "timer EndMatch keeps any old schedule: the changed one could not be armed: ...". A timer you did not change keeps its clock. **What you do:** run **Generate Server Code** on each type with a timer, then deploy; until you do, Server Compute marks it **Out of date** and refuses to deploy the project. See [Timers and events](../exec/access-members-and-timers.md#timers-and-events).
- **The limit on running Server Objects is documented.** An app with no funds can run 16 Server Objects at once, within 1 GB; a funded app 16,384, within 64 GB. Past it nothing new starts and calls come back **Unavailable**. For many players, prefer one shared object that holds a record per player (or per area, match or team) over one object per player. **What you do:** nothing. See [Large groups](../exec/access-members-and-timers.md#large-groups).
- **Trace lines and warnings are tidier.** With `crowdy.exec.trace` on, the Players Online root prints its missing Instance Id as `-` (`exec: root/- read ...`). Get Players Online's "has no count yet" warning prints once for each reason in each game instance, so once per Play In Editor client. **What you do:** nothing.
- **A voxel update with more than 1,024 bytes of state is refused when you send it.** The send returns false with "the voxel state is N octets, over the 1024 a voxel update carries", instead of reporting the update queued and then dropping it with a warning. **What you do:** keep a voxel's state at 1,024 bytes or less.
- **Records in Blueprint.** A Server Object that keeps [a record per entity](../exec/keep-a-record-per-entity.md) gains **Holds Records**, **Num Records**, **Watch Record** and **Stop Watching Record**, and the event **On Records Updated**. **Watch Record** takes a **Record Id** and an event (`FCrowdyServerRecordEvent`: **Object**, **Record Id**, **Changed**) that runs after each change of that record and when it is removed (**Find Record** is then false), and once at once when the record is already current; records dropped because the object **Failed** are not reported, **On Status Changed** is. **On Records Updated** (`RecordsUpdated`, an `FCrowdyServerRecordsUpdated`) is **On Records Changed** with each changed record's **Changed Variables**, which is empty when only its owner or team changed. **On Records Changed** is unchanged, and C++ already had `WatchRecord` and `OnRecordsChanged` with the changed fields. **What you do:** nothing. See [From Blueprint](../exec/keep-a-record-per-entity.md#from-blueprint).
- **Variables added in the asset are read and followed by the typed nodes.** For a definition whose variables are added in the asset (the List form), **Get**, **Get Server State** and **On Changed** read and follow them with the same pins as for a struct; this is now stated on the pages. **What you do:** nothing. See [Read and follow its variables](../exec/from-blueprint/read-and-follow-variables.md#get-a-variable).
- **Get Definition, and a widget without a component.** **Get Definition** is a new pure node on a Server Object, giving the definition asset it was made from, to pass to nodes that take one. A widget needs no component for a Server Object: **Get Server Object** with the widget as **Owner**, or a typed node with **Find By Asset**, already works, and the page now says so. **What you do:** nothing. See [Without the component](../exec/from-blueprint/get-a-server-object.md#without-the-component).
