A custom rendering backend can take part in the retry by overriding the new optional `UCrowdyRenderingBackend::IsInstanceActive`. **What you do:** nothing; raise `MaxPoolSizePerClass` if a pool warns it is at its cap. See [Rendering backends](../runtime/rendering-backends.md#configure-it).
- **A remote destroy no longer hands a still-live pool actor to another entity.** When a destroy event with a destroy delay arrived and the entity then left the tracker inside that delay, the pool actor went back to the pool, was given to the next entity, and was destroyed under it when the delay ran out, leaving that entity invisible until it timed out. The actor now stays with the destroy until it is gone, and an entity that keeps sending after its actor was destroyed is activated again. An actor's `EndPlay` also no longer removes the entity record of an actor that replaced it under the same id. **What you do:** nothing.
- **More trace lines for entities that do not appear.** `crowdy.entity.trace` now logs the success path too: "Spawn dispatched", "Spawn received" and "Entity registered", each with the id, class and location. `crowdy.pool.trace` logs each activation, each pool growth step, and each entity waiting at the cap. `crowdy.net.trace` logs every spatial message received (opcode, actor, chunk) and the transport's totals, so "the server never sent it" can be told apart from "the client dropped it". **What you do:** nothing; see [Troubleshooting](./troubleshooting.md#only-some-remote-entities-of-a-class-appear).
- **Known server issue: a player who just joined can stay invisible until they move.** The replication server refuses an actor's first update while it loads permissions, then accepts every later one but does not relay the actor to other players, or theirs to it, until it moves. The SDK sends what it should; this has been reported. See [Troubleshooting](./troubleshooting.md#a-player-who-just-joined-is-invisible-until-they-move).
- **A string value that changes only in letter case is now a change.** Unreal compares strings without regard to case by default, and the Game Model used that comparison to decide whether a value changed, so `alice` becoming `Alice` was never applied: the member kept the old spelling and no `CrowdyOnRep` or change delegate fired. It now applies like any other change, on pulls, confirmed invokes, and free containers. The same fix reaches the editor: Crowdy Studio's sync preview now shows a value, policy, or effect expression that changed only in case (it used to report nothing and never send it), the **Apply Effect** node keeps a string input you set to a different case of its default instead of dropping it, including after the Blueprint is reloaded, and the effect script editor keeps an edit that only changes case. **What you do:** nothing; the first sync after updating may upload a function whose stored text differs from your project only in case, once.
- **Your own invokes no longer pull back what they just wrote.** The notification the server sends for your own invoke used to be dropped once per container, so several quick invokes on one container pulled it again for all but the first. The SDK now expects one notification per invoke, counted when the request is sent, and drops that many, each expiring three seconds after its invoke; an invoke that fails or writes nothing gives its count back, and pulls instead if its notification was already dropped. Since a dropped notification could have been another client's write, a container that had one dropped is pulled once more within about three seconds. In the sandbox, a client invoking its own row ten times a second for a minute went from 118 pulls of that row to 29 (20 of them the three-second catch-up), with the watching client still pulling every change. `crowdy.gamemodel.stats` gains `SelfEchoMarksExpired` and `SelfEchoBackstopPulls`, and `SelfInvokesMarked` now counts invoke attempts sent (a retried invoke counts each attempt). **What you do:** nothing; another client's write to a container you are writing yourself can take up to about three seconds to show, where before it usually came with the next pull. See [Change pings and pull](../exec/move-from-game-models.md).
- **Your copies of other players' entities bind from one paged list per type, and first pulls after a bind are merged.** A remote proxy used to read its owner's row by key, one call each and again on every retry while the owner had not created it yet; it now joins the same paged list shared entities use, under the session active when it is listed, and one the list does not find yet waits for the next list instead of calling on its own. A copy never creates its owner's row. A copy-only list reads at most one page per copy it looks for; a type with more rows than that (an app-wide per-player type) is marked, and its copies read one key at a time from then on. The first pull after any container binds now waits the usual tenth of a second, so entities binding together read their state in one bulk call, and every entity bound to that container receives it; an invoke you send while that pull waits keeps its value when the pull lands. In the sandbox's two-client test, the observing client bound the same 40 copies with 10 list calls instead of 140 keyed reads, and the spawning client read the state of its 200 new containers in 10 calls instead of 200. `crowdy.gamemodel.bulkresolve`'s help now names remote copies, and `crowdy.gamemodel.stats` gains `BulkResolveListPages`. **What you do:** nothing; a newly bound entity may show its defaults up to a tenth of a second longer than before. See [Pre-seeding](../exec/move-from-game-models.md) and [Change pings and pull](../exec/move-from-game-models.md).
- **At most one state-applying pull per container is ever in flight, and a pull that would overlap it is held and merged instead of sent again.** A change notification, **Refresh Game Model** (`PullNow`), a first bind, or a bulk bind requested while a pull of that container is already out waits for it to land, then follows up: an explicit request (Refresh Game Model, a bulk bind) is sent right away, a notification or a first bind goes back through the usual tenth-of-a-second merge window. A bulk bind leaves out a container already being pulled. A read that never applies state (the combat kit's **Get Combatant State**, for example) is never held. `PullNow`'s tooltip now says it pulls now, or right after a read of that container already in flight lands, and `PullDataContainer`'s `OnDone` fires exactly once for the read that lands after the call, its own or the follow-up. Separately, a pull landing after your own invoke already wrote a newer value no longer rolls that value back: a key your invoke wrote after the pull was sent keeps the invoke's value, and if the pulled value actually differed, one follow-up pull is queued to re-converge the row; a key written before the pull is not protected, since the pull is newer. This does not cover another client's write landing in that same window, which still reaches you through the next notification as before. `crowdy.gamemodel.stats` gains `PullsHeldBehindInFlight`, `FollowUpPulls`, and `StaleKeysSkipped`, printed as `pulls held behind in flight N follow-ups N stale keys skipped N`; `OverlappingPulls` now counts only pulls that still applied state while another was out despite this, and should read near zero. **What you do:** nothing to keep working; a caller polling `PullNow` in a tight loop now gets fewer actual round trips for the same calls, not more state. See [Change pings and pull](../exec/move-from-game-models.md).
- **The SDK now retries a platform-busy refusal on its own before the caller ever sees a failure.** A query (a container state read, a bulk state read, a `ListContainers` page, or any other SDK query) resends on any refusal the platform blames on itself and marks retryable, except `WRONG_DATACENTER` (the SDK already follows that redirect) and `APP_UNAVAILABLE` (nowhere else to serve it). A container ensure and a `gameModelInvoke` resend only on `PLATFORM_BUSY`, the one code that means the work never started, so nothing is ever applied twice. At most 3 retries, waiting the server's suggested time when it names one (at least 0.1 s, plus up to 20% jitter, and not retried past 5 s) or a random 0.1-0.2 s doubled each time otherwise; at most 256 requests may be waiting out a backoff at once, past which a refusal goes straight to the caller. An invoke's busy retries run beside its existing rate-limit retry (`RATE_LIMITED`, 2 retries): the two caps are separate, and every attempt still counts toward the SDK's local invoke allowance window. `crowdy.net.retry.busy` (default 1, every build) turns it off, handing every refusal straight to the caller as before. `crowdy.gamemodel.stats` gains `Retries` / `RecoveredByRetry` per operation and an `invoke busy retries N recovered M gave up K` line (`InvokeBusyRetries` / `InvokeBusyRecovered` / `InvokeBusyGaveUp` on `UCrowdyGameModelSubsystem::GetNetStats`); a failure reason now counts only the final outcome, not each retried attempt. `UCrowdyGameModelSubsystem::IsBusyRefusal` and `FCrowdyCppJsonResult::Blame` / `bRetryable` / `RetryAfterMs` are new. **What you do:** nothing to keep working; a caller that built its own retry loop around a busy refusal is now retrying on top of the SDK's own retries. See [Console variables](../reference/console-cvars.md#behavior-switches), [Coalescing](../exec/move-from-game-models.md), and [Change pings and pull](../exec/move-from-game-models.md).
- **The SDK now asks for HTTP/2 on its own requests by default.** `crowdy.net.http2` (default 1, every build including Shipping, read per request) sets `IHttpRequest`'s HTTP version to `2TLS`, falling back to HTTP/1.1 when the server does not offer it; plain `http://` stays HTTP/1.1 regardless. Only the SDK's own requests are affected: the game's other HTTP traffic and the engine's `http.CurlAllowHTTP2` are untouched. On the test tier, multiplexing took a burst of 300 reads in 10 seconds from about 7.2 s p50 to 0.41 s, and stopped an unrelated call issued mid-burst from being delayed behind it. **What you do:** nothing to keep working, but read the caveat before you rely on the default: with HTTP/2 on, a request that fails at the network level (not a cancel or a timeout) can have its curl diagnostics logged at `Warning` with the request headers, bearer token included, in any build with logging enabled (a default Shipping build compiles logging out); set `crowdy.net.http2 0` if you ship or collect logs from a build with logging enabled. Faster delivery also means a burst reaches the server together, so expect more `PLATFORM_BUSY` refusals under heavy bursts; the SDK retries those on its own, see the busy-retry entry below. See [Console variables](../reference/console-cvars.md#behavior-switches) and [Change pings and pull](../exec/move-from-game-models.md).
- **`ListContainers` now reads every matching row instead of only the server's first page.** It pages the server 1000 rows at a time until a short page, up to 50 pages (50,000 rows), logging a warning if it stops there with more left unread; a failed page fails the whole call (`bOk` false, no partial list), and a row the server returns on two pages comes back once. For an app-scoped type, `SessionId` is now ignored the same way create and ensure already ignore it. `FCrowdyCppClient::ListContainers` at the bridge layer is unchanged and still returns one page. **What you do:** nothing to keep working, but a caller that assumed at most 200 rows back may now see more, and a caller that actually wanted only the first page has no way to ask for that anymore. See [Collections and Free Containers](../exec/move-from-game-models.md).
- **The invoke allowance governor now counts only invokes.** A pull, a list, an ensure, or any other Game Model read used to spend the same 120-per-10s allowance as a `gameModelInvoke`, which could stretch the coalesce merge window, the refresh-pull merge window, and container manifest pre-seeding under pure read traffic. Now an invoke is counted only when its request actually starts (a budget retry counts again); the coalesce window still widens as invokes approach the allowance, but the refresh-pull merge window no longer widens and manifest pre-seeding is no longer paced by the invoke count at all. **What you do:** nothing to keep working; a project whose pulls or a large manifest apply were being slowed down by the old shared counting should see that stop. See [Coalescing](../exec/move-from-game-models.md) and [Pre-seeding containers](../exec/move-from-game-models.md).
- **`crowdy.gamemodel.stats` splits each operation's latency into SDK time and HTTP time, breaks its failures down by reason, and adds in-flight and dispatched counts.** Each op row gains `SdkP50Ms` / `SdkP95Ms` (request created to handed off to the engine's HTTP module) and `HttpP50Ms` / `HttpP95Ms` (handed off to completion delivered, including any wait inside the HTTP module, the network, the server, and up to one frame for delivery); a cancelled request records no SDK/HTTP split. `FCrowdyGameModelOpStatsRow::FailureReasons` (and the log line's `failures: CODE xN, CODE xM`) counts each failure under the server's error code, or `graphql`, `http <status>`, `rejected`, `canceled`, or `transport` when there is none, up to eight reasons per op with the rest under `other`. Transport totals gain `InFlight` and `PeakInFlight`; net stats gain `InvokesDispatched`. No behavior changed. **What you do:** nothing; it is read-only, and a high HTTP time next to a low SDK time on the same op points at queueing inside the engine's HTTP module, not the SDK or the network. See [Change pings and pull](../exec/move-from-game-models.md).
- **New network diagnostics for the Game Model path.** `crowdy.gamemodel.stats` logs op calls, failures, and latency per server operation; pull counts and how many were redundant or overlapping; self-echo counts; resolves and re-resolves; invokes in the rate window beside the SDK's own governor count; transport bytes; the top pulled containers; and invoke faults by code, since the last reset. `crowdy.gamemodel.stats.reset` zeroes it. Both are new console commands, stripped from Shipping builds like the existing watch commands. The same numbers are on `UCrowdyGameModelSubsystem` in C++: `GetNetStats`, `ResetNetStats`, `GetInvokesInWindow`, `GetOpStats`, `DescribeNetStats`. No behavior changed. **What you do:** nothing; it is read-only. See [Change pings and pull](../exec/move-from-game-models.md) and [Console variables](../reference/console-cvars.md#diagnostic-commands).

## 2026-09-23 (SDK v2.16.0)

- **Backend gains a Test tier, and its default now follows the SDK build's own release tier.** `ECrowdyEnvironment` adds Test between Dev and Production, so the Backend selector on the Sign In page now offers Dev (shared), Test, Production, and Custom. The built-in hosts behind Dev and Production also moved, to `https://ck.dev.crowdedkingdoms.com` and `https://ck.prod.crowdedkingdoms.com`; the previous hosts, `api.dev.crowdedkingdoms.com` and `api.crowdedkingdoms.com`, no longer resolve, so a project left on Dev or Production with no Custom Discovery URL could not reach the backend. This release fixes that and adds `https://ck.test.crowdedkingdoms.com` for the new Test tier. Separately, a project's Backend used to default to Production until you ran Config Sync; it now defaults to the tier this SDK build was released for (Dev on a dev build, Test on a test build, Production on the public release), and the Discovery URL default follows the same tier instead of always pointing at Dev. Each tier also vendors its own CrowdyCPP build (0.42.1), so a connection opened with no origin configured at all dials that tier's host directly; a released build dials `ck.prod.crowdedkingdoms.com`. **What you do:** nothing if your `DefaultGame.ini` already names an `Environment`, which it does for any project that has used the Backend selector; that value is unaffected. A brand-new project now connects out of the box on whichever tier's build you are running, instead of defaulting to a Production host you may not have an app on. A new static C++ read, `UCrowdySDKDeveloperSettings::GetReleaseEnvironment()`, returns the tier a build defaults to; it is not exposed to Blueprint. See [Project settings](../reference/project-settings.md#the-default-backend) and [Installation](../installation.md#step-6-connect-your-app).

## 2026-09-22 (SDK v2.15.0)

**Six changes.** One is a source break for C++ projects; two remove work you may have done; one moves the moment a player pawn gets its identity; one changes how inbound traffic is signed and needs nothing from you; one is a Crowdy Studio panel. The examples on this site are written for 2.15.0.

- **Crowdy Studio shows every value a live model holds.** The Live tab's one-line summary, which named the first few attributes and then said "and N more", is now a panel under the instance list: one row per attribute with its value, what it holds, and its description, plus the attributes the model declares that the live model has no value for, a search box over names and values, **Copy value** and **Copy values**, and an **Internal** switch for the runtime's own keys. The page's **Pre-seed containers** strip hides itself while the Live tab is open, so the list and the panel get its height. **What you do:** nothing; it is an editor panel.

- **Inbound bundles arrive with one signature per datagram.** The transport now tells the replication server what it can read (a `CLIENT_CAPABILITIES` message, sent once the connection is up and every 15 seconds after), and a server at v0.30.0 or later answers by packing its notifications into `MESSAGE_BUNDLE_SIGNED` datagrams: one HMAC over the whole bundle instead of one per member. The messages your handlers receive are the same; only the verification cost per datagram drops. Up to and including 2.14.0 every member carried and was checked against its own signature, and an older server still does that. **What you do:** nothing. `crowdy.net.recv.signedbundles 0` turns the advertisement off for a diagnostic comparison, read when a connection opens like `crowdy.net.send.bundle`. See [Connection and reconnect](../runtime/connection-and-reconnect.md#signed-inbound-bundles).

- **Eighteen array delegates pass `const TArray<T>&` instead of `TArray<T>` by value.** Ten single-cast: `FOnTeamsSuccess`, `FOnTeamMembersSuccess`, `FOnTeamRolesSuccess`, `FOnMyTeamsSuccess` (teams), `FOnAvatarsSuccess`, `FOnAppStatesSuccess` (avatars), `FOnChannelsSuccess`, `FOnChannelMembersSuccess`, `FOnChannelRolesSuccess`, `FOnMyChannelsSuccess` (channels). Three multicast cache events a 2.1 project is likely to have bound with `AddDynamic`: `FOnMyTeamsCacheChanged`, `FOnMyAvatarsCacheChanged`, `FOnMyChannelsCacheChanged`. Five Game Model outcome events, for a project that adopted collections or sessions on 2.13 or 2.14: `FCrowdyCollectionItemsOutcome`, `FCrowdyTraverseOutcome` (both parameters), `FCrowdyContainerRefsOutcome`, `FCrowdySessionsOutcome`, `FCrowdySessionEventsOutcome`. **What you do:** on 2.15.0, any C++ `UFUNCTION` bound to one of them changes its parameter from `TArray<FCrowdyTeam> Teams` to `const TArray<FCrowdyTeam>& Teams`, and likewise for the rest. A Blueprint custom event bound to one of these pins is unaffected; Blueprint has no by-value versus by-reference distinction on the pin.

:::warning[This is a source break, not a behavior change]
A C++ project that takes 2.15.0 and rebuilds gets a compile error naming the handler's parameter. Nothing changes silently: if the project builds, it is right. On 2.14.0 and earlier the delegates pass by value, so a handler changed before you update fails to bind for the same reason.
:::

- **The actor pool draws with no Backend Config at all.** Up to and including 2.14.0, a map profile whose Backend Config was empty, or whose config named no Replication Policy Class, left remote Dynamic entities tracked but never rendered, so choosing a Backend Config was mandatory in practice. In 2.15.0 a missing config falls back to a built-in transform-interpolation policy, `UCrowdyTransformRepPolicy`, and that step is optional. **What you do:** nothing. A project that authored its own Backend Config is unaffected; a project that left it empty and worked around the blank screen can delete the workaround once it is on 2.15.0. See [Map profile](../runtime/map-profile.md) and [Rendering backends](../runtime/rendering-backends.md).
- **The shipped transform policy interpolates across a ring of samples.** Up to and including 2.14.0, `UCrowdyTransformRepPolicy` kept two samples per proxy: it snapped to a lone sample, blended between the two it held, and stopped at the newer one when the render time passed it, so a late update showed as a pause and the next as a jump. In 2.15.0 it keeps a ring of recent samples per proxy in `TInterpolatedField`, samples the pair that brackets the render time, and extrapolates from the last two for at most 0.2 seconds when the render time runs past the newest. **What you do:** nothing. Proxies drawn by the shipped policy move more smoothly through late and lost updates. A project that wrote its own policy to get that behavior can drop it, or rebuild it on `TInterpolatedField` and keep its extra fields; see [Rendering backends](../runtime/rendering-backends.md#the-sample-ring).
- **A Player Derived pawn possessed after it begins play gets its account identity on possession, respawned pawns included.** Up to and including 2.14.0, `UCrowdyEntityComponent` read the Player Derived identity once, in `BeginPlay`, and the engine possesses a pawn spawned during play (`RestartPlayer`, a respawn, a spawn from a connected handler) only after that, so every runtime-spawned player pawn registered under a random id with one warning, and whatever is keyed on the local player id (the host lookup, ownership requests, the drop of your own echoed events) never worked for it; only a pawn possessed before `BeginPlay` got the account identity. In 2.15.0 a Player Derived pawn with no controller at `BeginPlay` waits, and registers under the account id inside its first possession, after the pawn's own Possessed and Controller Changed events; the first controller of any kind completes it (an AI controller gets the old fallback and warning), a later unpossess or repossess changes nothing, and a respawn that leaves the earlier pawn alive hands the id to the new pawn and clears the old one, which stops replicating. **What you do:** read the pawn's id and `IsLocallyOwned()` from `OnCrowdyOwnershipAssigned` (**On Crowdy Ownership Assigned**) or the entity subsystem's `OnEntityRegistered`, not from `BeginPlay` or Possessed: on 2.15.0 a pawn graph that gates on **Is Locally Owned** at `BeginPlay` reads false and runs nothing, where on 2.14.0 it ran with the random id. A pawn that begins play before the sign-in has answered is unchanged: it derives from user id 0 without a warning, so keep the spawn behind **On UDP Connection Success**. See [Quickstart](../quickstart.md#1-make-your-player-a-crowdy-entity) and [Entities, Identity, and Ownership](../concepts/entities-identity-ownership.md#identity-policies).

## 2026-09-17 (SDK v2.14.0)

**Everything in 2.14.0 is additive.** No game-facing function, pin, or type was renamed or removed, so a project on 2.0 / 2.1 has no required action for this release. Four things are new.

- **Sessions can seed from app-scoped rows.** `FCrowdyGameModelCreateSessionOptions` gained `SeedFromAppTypeNames` (container types whose keyed app-scoped rows are copied into the new session as it is created) and `SeedInitialState` (`ECrowdySessionSeedState`: `Defaults` or `App`, sent only when the type list is non-empty). The create response carries `SeededContainerCount`, valid when `bHasSeededContainerCount` is set. **Create Game Session** exposes all of them. Each seeded type must be admin-instantiable or carry a bind policy; the whole create is refused otherwise.
- **Container states pull in bulk.** The subsystem reads many containers in one call, up to 500 per request, chunked automatically past that, for a caller that already holds the id set. It is what **Get Collection With Items' State** uses instead of one pull per item.
- **A container type can be app-scoped.** `meta=(CrowdyContainer="X", CrowdyScope="App")` declares one row per key for the whole app, bound with no session. The default is session-scoped and unchanged. An app-scoped type never takes a session id; naming one on it is refused with the code `CONTAINER_TYPE_APP_SCOPED`, which **Get Last Crowdy Model Error Code** returns. Worth doing on a project that has a shared, admin- or player-owned container every client used to race to create: declare it `CrowdyInstantiableBy="Admin"` and pre-seed it from Crowdy Studio.
- **The active session survives opening a new map.** **Set Active Crowdy Session** (`SetActiveSession`) now persists on the Game Instance, and a new map reads it back when it loads. A **Leave** or **End** of the active session forgets it, as does **Clear Active Crowdy Session** (`ClearActiveSession`). Before 2.14.0 a fresh map never inherited a session. **What you do:** when a match ends, leave or end its session, or call **Clear Active Crowdy Session**, before you open the next map.

:::warning[A map loaded after a finished match binds into that match unless you clear the session]
A game that never clears the active session between matches loads its next map with placed shared containers still bound into the ended match's session instead of the app-global scope. Reads return the stale session's rows, and writes go there. Leave, end, or clear on the way out of every match.
:::

## 2026-09-15 (SDK v2.13.0)

**Game Model sessions are new.** The July SDK had no `game-models` section and no session concept; 2.13.0 adds both. `UCrowdyGameModelSubsystem` creates, joins, leaves, ends, locks, and transfers host on a session (`CreateSession`, `JoinSession`, `LeaveSession`, `EndSession`, `SetSessionAdmission`, `TransferSessionHost`, `WatchSession`), with presence per participant and a typed change stream on **On Game Session Changed** (`OnSessionChanged`). The Blueprint category is **Crowdy SDK, Game Model, Sessions & Turns**.

- **What changed:** authoritative, cheat-sensitive state (HP, inventory, scores, match rules) has a server-owned home, a Game Model container, and a match has a server-owned lifetime, a session. Neither existed in the SDK you integrated. High-frequency view state (movement, animation) stays where it was, in CrowdyState; the two do not merge.
- **Session words are enums.** `FCrowdyGameModelSession::Status` is an `ECrowdySessionStatus`; admission is `ECrowdySessionAdmission`; presence is `ECrowdySessionPresence`; the reason a session ended is `ECrowdySessionEndReason`, and the reason a participant left is `ECrowdySessionLeftReason`. Each has a matching filter enum where a query takes one (`ECrowdySessionStatusFilter`, `ECrowdySessionAdmissionFilter`). In Blueprint, a **Switch on ECrowdySessionStatus** branches on a status; there is no string to compare.
- **What you do otherwise:** nothing is required. A project that keeps its gameplay state in its own code keeps working.

## 2026-09-15 (SDK v2.12.0)

**Outbound messages are bundled.** Several messages the SDK sends in the same pass now travel in one datagram instead of one datagram each. The switch is the CVar `crowdy.net.send.bundle`, default `1`, read when a connection opens. No API changed and nothing you send looks different to your handlers.

- **What you do on a current replication server:** nothing.
- **What you do on a replication server older than v0.27.0:** upgrade the server, or set `crowdy.net.send.bundle 0` in `DefaultEngine.ini` (`[ConsoleVariables]`) until you can. An older server does not unpack a bundle, so a bundled pair is dropped without an error. If reliable events start arriving in ones and not in pairs after the update, this is the first thing to check. See [Console CVars](../reference/console-cvars.md).

## 2026-08-30 (SDK, sign-in)

**The dev-only sign-in bypass is gone.** `UCrowdyAuthentication::DevLogin`, email-only sign-in against a server flagged for it and never usable in production, is removed from the SDK; the server stopped accepting it on 2026-08-20. It does not exist as a deprecated stub; a call to it does not compile.

- **What changed:** `Login(Email, Password, ...)` and `Register(Email, Password, ...)` work against every tier, including a local or development server, and are the replacement for any scripted sign-in. Magic link (`BeginMagicLinkSignIn`) and social sign-in (`BeginSocialSignIn`) are unchanged.
- **What you do:** replace each `DevLogin` call with `Login` or `Register` and supply a real password. For a headless test client, register a dedicated account once and store its password the way you store any other secret, never in the project.
- **Email + password is first-class and permanent.** If the July pages left you expecting passwordless sign-in to replace it, they should not have: password sign-in sits beside magic link and social as an equal method and has no removal planned. Nothing about it changed between 2.1 and 2.14. See [Authentication](../services/authentication.md).

:::warning[A build script or CI job that signs in with DevLogin breaks at the next SDK update]
Switch it to `Login` or `Register` with a real password before you update the plugin, not after. The failure is a compile error in your code, so a job that builds the project fails before it ever signs in.
:::

## Between 2.1.0 and 2.12.0 (SDK)

Changes that shipped between the July plugin and v2.12.0. A project moving from 2.1 to any later release meets all of them at once.

- **Teams types are named for teams, not groups.** `FCrowdyGroup`, `FCrowdyGroupMember`, `FCrowdyGroupMembership`, `FCrowdyGroupRole`, `FCrowdyRolePermissions` and `FCrowdyAppGroupPolicy` are now `FCrowdyTeam`, `FCrowdyTeamMember`, `FCrowdyTeamMembership`, `FCrowdyTeamRole`, `FCrowdyTeamPermissions` and `FCrowdyTeamPolicy`, and their members followed: `GroupId` to `TeamId`, `GroupMemberId` to `TeamMemberId`, `GroupRoleId` to `TeamRoleId`, `Membership.Group` to `Team`, `bManageGroup` to `bManageTeam`, `MaxGroupsPerUser` to `MaxTeamsPerUser`, `FCrowdyTeamsResult.Groups` to `Teams`, `FCrowdyChannelsResult.Groups` to `Channels`, and the enumerator `ECrowdyTeamPermission::ManageGroup` to `ManageTeam`. **What you do:** in C++, rename; a handler such as `OnCacheChanged(TArray<FCrowdyGroupMembership>)` or a read of `Team.GroupId` no longer compiles. Blueprint assets follow the plugin's own CoreRedirects and need only a resave, except a node whose function parameter was renamed (`GroupId` to `TeamId` on the `UCrowdyTeams` calls): open that graph once and reconnect the renamed pin. See [Teams](../services/teams.md) and [Packaging](./packaging.md#6-coreredirects-ship-with-the-plugin).
- **`SetManagementApiUrl` is gone; `SetDiscoveryUrl` replaces it.** `UCrowdySDKSubsystem::SetManagementApiUrl` has no counterpart and no redirect. **What you do:** call `SetDiscoveryUrl` for the shared origin, or `SetGameApiUrl` for the gameplay endpoint; in Blueprint the old node is missing on load and is replaced by hand. See [Project settings](../reference/project-settings.md).
- **The query and subscription subsystems are gone.** `UCrowdyQuerySubsystem` and `UCrowdySubscriptionSubsystem` (their `Connect`, `ExecuteQuery`, `GetSubscriptionState` calls and `OnConnected`, `OnDisconnected`, `OnGetVersionInfo`, `OnTeleport` events) do not exist. GraphQL now goes through the service subsystems. **What you do:** remove the calls; a Blueprint that used them has missing nodes on load. The services pages ([Teams](../services/teams.md), [Avatars](../services/avatars.md), [Authentication](../services/authentication.md)) are where the same data comes from now.
- **The C++ reception-layer interface is gone.** `ICrowdyReceptionLayer` and `UCrowdySDKSubsystem::RegisterReceptionLayer` / `IsLayerRegistered` are removed. **What you do:** a C++ system that implemented the interface subscribes instead: `UCrowdySDKSubsystem::SubscribeToEventPayload`, `SubscribeToActorUpdatePayload`, `SubscribeToAllPayloads` and `SubscribeToOpcode` return an `FCrowdySubscription` handle that delivers for as long as it lives. The Blueprint **Crowdy Blueprint Reception Layer** is unchanged; see [Recipients and routing](../runtime/recipients-and-routing.md).
- **The connection monitor is no longer part of the documented path.** `UCrowdySDKSubsystem` retries a dropped UDP connection on its own and broadcasts **On UDP Timed Out** when a re-assignment failed and **On UDP Connection Success** when the connection is back. A project that also calls `InitConnectionMonitor` runs a second, redundant retry loop beside the SDK's. Five functions on `UCrowdySDKSubsystem` are deprecated. Three do nothing: `StartUDPTimeoutMonitoring`, `TriggerUdpHeartbeat`, `DeregisterAllReceptionLayers`. `StopUDPTimeoutMonitoring` only stops the latency ping, and `SetQueryEndpoint` forwards to `SetGameApiUrl`. **What you do:** bind the two events in your Game Instance's `Init`, remove every call to `InitConnectionMonitor` and to the first four, and replace `SetQueryEndpoint` with `SetGameApiUrl` or `SetDiscoveryUrl`. The compiler warns on each deprecated call, so a build log lists them for you. See [Connection and reconnect](../runtime/connection-and-reconnect.md#deprecated-calls).
- **A project that configures no map profile now runs networked.** The plugin registers a shipped default profile, so a map with no `MapProfiles` entry and no `DefaultProfile` resolves to it: networking on, the actor pool as backend. In 2.1 such a map went inactive. **What you do:** nothing if you have profiles; if you relied on an unlisted map being inactive, give it a profile with **Enable Networking** off. See [Map profile](../runtime/map-profile.md).

## Persistence

**`UCrowdyPersistenceSubsystem` is deprecated in these docs.** The push / pull of tagged gameplay structs over UDP and GraphQL that the July `services/persistence` page described still exists in the SDK, with its three callables `PushState`, `PullState`, and `ClearAllState` (and the Blueprint **Push State** / **Pull State** wildcards), and it keeps working in 2.14. It receives no further development, and no removal date is set. The plugin does not mark it, so no compiler or Blueprint warning appears. The two struct tags it reads, `CrowdyPersistent` (push and pull this struct) and `CrowdySingleton` (one slot, not one per instance), are still honored and go with it.

- **What you do:** nothing today. When you touch that code next, move the state into your app's server code on [ck-exec](/exec/intro), which is what persistence was standing in for. Authoritative and cheat-sensitive state belongs on the server, never in CrowdyState; see [The Two Planes](../concepts/two-planes.md).
- **What not to do:** do not start a new feature on `PushState`. Server code gives you the same durable, per-subject state plus server-side validation, and it is where the effort goes.

## Gotchas

- For a C++ project on 2.14.0 the source breaks are the teams rename, the removals listed under "Between 2.1.0 and 2.12.0", and `DevLogin`. If your project builds clean against 2.14.0 after those, nothing else here is blocking; the array delegates come with the next release.
- A Blueprint project's exposure is the renamed `GroupId` pins on the teams calls, the missing `DevLogin`, `SetManagementApiUrl`, query and subscription nodes on load, the persistence nodes (still present, no warning) and the connection-monitor nodes (still present, marked deprecated).
- `crowdy.net.send.bundle 0` is a compatibility switch for an old server, not a debugging aid. Leave it at `1` on a current server.
- The [sample project](./sample-project.md) targets SDK 2.1.0 and predates every entry on this page; its tour is a 2.1 tour.

# Classes and Subsystems
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/reference/subsystems

# Classes and Subsystems

The consumer-facing classes you fetch most, with the module they live in and where to read more. The manifest carries 31 classes tagged as subsystems; 8 are excluded here because they are internal plumbing or deprecated, listed at the bottom of this page for completeness.

## When you come here

You know the shape of what you need (send an event, read a team, elect a host) but not which class owns it, or you want the one-line reminder of what a class you already use is for.

:::note[Every subsystem here initializes automatically. You fetch it, you never create one.]
:::

## Fetching a subsystem

How you fetch a subsystem depends on its scope. Game instance subsystems come from the game instance, world subsystems come from the world.

Game instance subsystems:

```cpp
UCrowdySDKSubsystem* SDK = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UCrowdySDKSubsystem>();
UCrowdyTeams* Teams = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UCrowdyTeams>();
```

World subsystems:

```cpp
UCrowdyEntitySubsystem* Entities = GetWorld()->GetSubsystem<UCrowdyEntitySubsystem>();
```

Blueprint function libraries (`UCrowdyUtilities`, `UCrowdyStateBlueprintLibrary`, `UCrowdyOwnershipTransfer`, `UCrowdyReplicatedSubsystemLibrary`) are static and need no fetch; see [Entities and spawning](../runtime/entities-and-spawning.md), [Marking state from outside the actor](../runtime/crowdy-state.md#marking-state-from-outside-the-actor), [Ownership transfer](../runtime/ownership-transfer.md) and [Replicated subsystems](../runtime/replicated-subsystems.md).

## Excluded from this table

Eight of the manifest's 31 subsystem classes do not appear in the table above:

- `UCrowdyCppClientSubsystem`, `UCrowdyCppReplicationSubsystem`, `UCrowdySDKBridgeSubsystem`, `UCrowdyWorkerThreadsSubsystem`: the vendored CrowdyCPP bridge and its worker threads. The game-facing surface is `UCrowdySDKSubsystem`; see [Connection and reconnect](../runtime/connection-and-reconnect.md).
- `UCrowdyConnectionMonitor`: the SDK reconnects on its own after a timeout, so starting the monitor adds a second retry loop. What it reports is covered on [Connection and reconnect](../runtime/connection-and-reconnect.md).
- Two test harnesses in the Mass module that the SDK uses to verify itself. They are not part of the surface a game uses.
- `UCrowdyPersistenceSubsystem`: superseded by server code on ck-exec; still present and working, and the plugin does not mark it deprecated. It reads the `CrowdyPersistent` and `CrowdySingleton` struct tags. See [What's Changed](../guides/whats-changed.md#persistence) for what still works and what does not get further development.

## Gotchas

- A world subsystem needs a valid world; fetch it after `BeginPlay`, not in a constructor.
- Read the Outer column for scope; the class name does not always say it (`UCrowdyGameSession` is a game instance subsystem, `UCrowdyHostSubsystem` a world one).
- `UCrowdySDKDeveloperSettings` looks like it belongs here but is not a subsystem at all; it lives on [Project Settings](./project-settings.md).

- [Host authority](../runtime/host-authority.md)
- [Connection and reconnect](../runtime/connection-and-reconnect.md)
- [What's Changed](../guides/whats-changed.md#persistence)

# Blueprint Async Actions
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/reference/async-actions

# Blueprint Async Actions

A Blueprint async action is a latent node: it keeps running after the graph moves on and fires one of its own exec pins when it finishes. The SDK ships 60 of them, one C++ class each. One, the class behind the typed Call node of a Server Object, has no palette entry of its own, so the table lists the other 59. Every one listed is covered by the pages below, so this table is a lookup, not a gap list.

## When you come here

You have a node open in the graph and want the page that explains its inputs, or you remember a page and want the exact node name to search for in the palette.

The **Blueprint node** column is the title you see in the Blueprint editor, taken from the factory function's display name. The **C++ factory** column is the static function that creates the action, and the **Class** column is the C++ class behind it; you need those only for a `Cast` or a manual `Activate` call from C++, since the whole point of an async action is that Blueprint drives it. **Completion pins** lists the node's output exec pins in order, so you know which ones to wire before you drop the node.

<SurfaceTable table="async-actions" group="page" />

:::note[Every row above links forward. There is nothing left uncovered in this table.]
Coverage for the 59 listed is complete: every one is mentioned on the page its row links to. A class that later stops matching any page (a rename, a page deleted) reopens as a coverage gap, not a silent removal from this table.
:::

## Gotchas

- The node's display name, its factory function and its C++ class name can all differ (the **Call Server Function** node is `UCrowdyServerCallAction`); search the palette by the **Blueprint node** column, not the **Class** column.
- A latent node only fires its completion pins while the graph that called it is still alive. A widget removed from its parent before the call completes never sees the result.
- An async action with no ID pin operates on whatever the node's own inputs named at spawn time; it does not automatically track a Target that changes after the call starts.

## Related

- [Subsystems](./subsystems.md)
- [Delegates](./delegates.md)
- [RPC Events in Blueprint](../runtime/rpc-events-blueprint.md)

# Blueprint Delegates
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/reference/delegates

# Blueprint Delegates

A dynamic multicast delegate is what you bind with **Bind Event to** or **Assign** in Blueprint, or `AddDynamic` in C++. The SDK exposes 167 of them; 2 belong to a private actor a game cannot reference and are dropped from this table, and 1 more, `UCrowdyConnectionMonitor::OnConnectionStateChanged`, is left out because the SDK reconnects on its own. So 164 rows render below.

## When you come here

You have a delegate bound and want to know what its parameters mean, or you know roughly what you want to react to and want the class that fires it.

All 164 delegates below fire on the game thread. This is a constant fact about every dynamic multicast delegate the SDK broadcasts, never a per-delegate choice, so it is stated once here instead of as a column that would read the same value 164 times: your handler runs like any other Blueprint event or `UFUNCTION`, with no thread-safety code of your own to write.

<SurfaceTable table="delegates" group="owner" />

:::note[OnConnectionStateChanged is not in the table.]
`UCrowdyConnectionMonitor::OnConnectionStateChanged` is not part of the documented path: the SDK reconnects on its own, and starting the monitor adds a second retry loop. Binding it to observe the connection state is safe; do not build retry logic on it. See [Connection and reconnect](../runtime/connection-and-reconnect.md).
:::

## Gotchas

- A delegate's owner class must be reachable before you can bind it: a game instance subsystem's delegate is safe to bind in a C++ Game Instance's `Init` after `Super::Init()`, and in Blueprint from the Game Mode's Event BeginPlay (the Game Instance's Event Init runs before the subsystems exist); a world subsystem's needs a valid world first.
- Binding twice fires your handler twice. Unbind (`Remove Dynamic` or `RemoveDynamic`) before a re-bind on a path that can run more than once, such as a widget that reconstructs.
- Two delegates on `AWinAudioDeviceMonitor` exist in the SDK but are not shown here: that actor is private and spawned by the voice subsystem for itself, so a game never has a reference to bind against. See [Voice chat](../services/voice-chat.md).

## Related

- [Subsystems](./subsystems.md)
- [Async actions](./async-actions.md)
- [Connection and reconnect](../runtime/connection-and-reconnect.md)

# Console Variables
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/reference/console-cvars

# Console Variables

This page lists 51 `crowdy.*` console entries. They come in three kinds: trace gates that turn on
informational logging for one area, behavior switches that change what the SDK does, and diagnostic
commands that run once and hold no stored value. A row badged **Editor only** exists only in the editor
process. Five of the diagnostic commands (`crowdy.rpc.dumpfn`, `crowdy.state.heartbeat.advisories`,
`crowdy.registry.dump`, `crowdy.mass.derive`, `crowdy.mass.state.verdict`) and every other `crowdy.mass.*` entry are compiled out of
a Shipping build and are absent there rather than silent; every other row ships in Development and Shipping.

## When you land here

You want to know what a `crowdy.*` name does before you type it, or you are looking for the switch that
turns on a specific area's logging. For the workflow around them (loopback testing, two-PIE setups), see
[Testing locally](../guides/testing-locally.md); this page is the lookup table.

## Trace gates

All 19 are off by default. Seventeen turn on that area's informational lines when set to `1`; the two
`.scopes` entries add Unreal Insights CPU scopes instead and log nothing. Warnings and errors print
regardless of the setting.

<SurfaceTable table="cvars" filter="role=trace" includeEditor />

:::caution[`crowdy.serialize.trace` and `crowdy.serialize.scopes` are high frequency.]
They log on every message encode and decode. Leave them off unless you are actively debugging
serialization.
:::

:::caution[`crowdy.net.trace` logs every routed send and every received spatial message.]
Since 2.17.0 it also prints one line per spatial message received ("Received opcode ... for actor ... in chunk
...") and the transport's totals (datagrams received, verification failures, drops) about once a second. That
is what tells "the server never sent it" apart from "the client dropped it"; it is too chatty to leave on.
:::

:::note[`crowdy.serialize.scopes` and `crowdy.state.scopes` are nested CPU trace scopes.]
Each nests inside a wider enclosing scope, so turning one on shifts the timing you read for that
enclosing scope too. If you are taking a performance reading, say whether the flag was on.
:::

`crowdy.studio.trace` and `crowdy.mass.nodes.trace` are editor only. `crowdy.studio.trace` never logs the
bearer token, a pattern worth copying in your own logging around Studio calls.

## Behavior switches

These change what the SDK does rather than what it logs. None of the 24 exist only in the editor.

<SurfaceTable
  table="cvars"
  filter="role=behaviour"
  notes={{
    "crowdy.net.receive.maxmessages": "How many inbound replication messages one frame may deliver; whatever is left waits for the next frame. Default 3072.",
    "crowdy.net.receive.maxdrainms": "How many milliseconds of one frame may be spent delivering inbound messages. Raise the message count first. Default 4.",
    "crowdy.net.send.bundle": "Pack one network pass's outbound messages into one datagram. Needs a replication server of v0.27.0 or later; against an older one every bundled message is dropped together. Default 1, read when a connection opens.",
    "crowdy.net.recv.signedbundles": "Tell the replication server this client reads signed inbound bundles, so notifications arrive with one signature per datagram instead of one per member. A server older than v0.30.0 ignores it. Default 1, read when a connection opens.",
    "crowdy.replication.tracker.maxgatheredupdates": "How many actor updates for already-tracked actors may be gathered before the backlog is discarded; reached only when the world tick is not consuming them. Default 8192.",
    "crowdy.replication.tracker.maxqueuedupdates": "How many updates for actors not yet on screen may wait for a worker thread before further ones are dropped, counted, and reported once a second; reached only when the worker pool is not draining them. A dropped actor appears on a later update. Default 8192."
  }}
  notesLabel="Where the Help cell is empty"
/>

The notes map above stands in for these six rows because the surface exporter drops a CVar help built from adjacent `TEXT()` literals.

:::warning[Turn `crowdy.net.http2` off if you ship, or collect logs from, a build with logging enabled.]
On by default, it asks for HTTP/2 on the SDK's own requests (falling back to HTTP/1.1 when the server does not offer it); the game's other HTTP traffic and the engine's `http.CurlAllowHTTP2` are untouched. With HTTP/2, when a request fails at the network level (not a cancel or a timeout), the curl diagnostics the engine logs at `Warning` can include the request headers, bearer token included. A default Shipping build compiles logging out, so most projects never see this; if yours ships or collects logs from a build with logging enabled, set `crowdy.net.http2 0`.
:::

:::note[`crowdy.net.retry.busy` resends a refusal the platform blames on itself before the caller ever sees `Failed`.]
On by default. An SDK query resends on any platform-blamed retryable refusal except `WRONG_DATACENTER` and `APP_UNAVAILABLE`. At most 3 retries, with the server's suggested wait when it names one or a doubling local wait otherwise. Password sign-in, the app token mint and the app token refresh are retried the same way when the platform answers that it is busy, and a retried request is dropped if the account's token changed meanwhile. Registration, link and social completion, password changes, email sends, logout and account deletion are never retried. Turn it off (`0`) only to compare against the un-retried behavior; leave it on for a shipping build.
:::

:::note[`crowdy.kit.emotes.*` cap the emotes a client will read, per sender and across all senders.]
Each sender has its own small budget, and every emote also has to fit one budget shared across all senders. `crowdy.kit.emotes.persender.maxpersecond` (default 4) is how fast one sender's budget refills; `crowdy.kit.emotes.persender.burst` (default 4) is the most it holds. The per-sender budget is checked first, so one player flooding emotes runs out of their own budget and no longer uses up the shared one. An emote the shared budget drops costs its sender nothing. A client tracks at most 256 senders, and when that is full the sender that has been silent longest is forgotten.

The shared budget exists because a sender id is only what the sender claims. `crowdy.kit.emotes.maxpersecond` (default 64) is how fast it refills; `crowdy.kit.emotes.burst` (default 16) is the most it holds. An emote over either budget is dropped before it is read, with one Warning in the log. A peer that forges a player's id can use up that player's per-sender budget, which costs that player nothing but their own emotes. Raise the numbers only if a busy scene legitimately sends more emotes than that. See [Send an emote](../services/play-together.md#send-an-emote).
:::

:::warning[Leave `crowdy.rpc.allowObjectLoad` off in production.]
While it is off, an untrusted peer cannot trigger an arbitrary asset load; an unresolved object or class
reference in a received RPC is delivered as null instead.
:::

`crowdy.rpc.loopback` and `crowdy.state.loopback` are not the same switch wearing two names.
`crowdy.rpc.loopback` delivers a sent event back to your own receive path. `crowdy.state.loopback` cannot
replay onto the same actor that sent the delta: an owner's own entity drops a non-host-sourced delta, and
changed-detection on decode sees no change against identical values. Instead it spawns a distinct,
lazily-created mirror entity and replays deltas onto that, so `CrowdyOnRep` still fires with one PIE
client. Expect two entities, not one, when you turn it on.

`crowdy.net.receive.poolactorupdates` defaults to `1` (pooling on). Turning it off is for an A/B
measurement against the same build, not a fix for anything.

## Diagnostic commands

Eight commands with no stored value. Only `crowdy.rpc.dumpfn` and `crowdy.mass.derive` take arguments and
print usage without them; every other command acts as soon as you run it. Five are compiled out of a Shipping
build: `crowdy.rpc.dumpfn`, `crowdy.state.heartbeat.advisories`, `crowdy.registry.dump`, `crowdy.mass.derive` and
`crowdy.mass.state.verdict`. `crowdy.registry.dump` logs every entry the cook baked into the registry, one
line each: the structs and their layout hashes, the CrowdyState properties, and the CrowdyEvent functions,
with their ids. It is the console version of the Registry page (see [Inspector and Registry](../studio/inspector-and-registry.md)).

<SurfaceTable
  table="cvars"
  filter="role=command"
  includeEditor
  notes={{
    "crowdy.rpc.dumpfn": "Not in Shipping",
    "crowdy.state.heartbeat.advisories": "Not in Shipping",
    "crowdy.registry.dump": "Not in Shipping",
    "crowdy.mass.derive": "Not in Shipping",
    "crowdy.mass.state.verdict": "Not in Shipping",
    "crowdy.cpp.selftest": "Every build",
    "crowdy.net.routes": "Every build"
  }}
  notesLabel="Build"
/>

:::tip[`crowdy.rpc.dumpfn` and `crowdy.state.heartbeat.advisories` print structured text you can paste directly into a bug report.]
:::

The development-build sign-in commands `crowdy.auth.signin.file`, `crowdy.auth.status` and `crowdy.auth.signout` are described under [Sign in from the console](../guides/testing-locally.md#sign-in-from-the-console).

`crowdy.cpp.selftest` and `crowdy.net.routes` carry no build guard, so they exist in every build including
Shipping; the four diagnostics above do not, and a Shipping console answers them with an unknown command.

## Gotchas

- Warnings and errors are never gated behind a trace flag. They print under the module's log category no
  matter what.
- `crowdy.net.receive.maxdrainms` (4 ms) and `crowdy.net.receive.maxmessages` (3072) bound one frame's
  receive drain. If drains keep ending on the time budget, delivery is costing more per message than the
  frame can afford, and raising the count is not the lever.

## Related

- [Project settings](./project-settings.md): the settings-class properties that sit beside these CVars.
- [Testing locally](../guides/testing-locally.md): loopback and two-PIE workflows built on these switches.

# Project Settings
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/reference/project-settings

# Project Settings

The SDK's settings live on `UCrowdySDKDeveloperSettings`, under **Project Settings, Plugins, Crowdy SDK**.
It is written to `Config/DefaultGame.ini` under `[/Script/CrowdyReplication.CrowdySDKDeveloperSettings]`.
None of it is secret; commit the file as usual.

## When you land here

You are looking for a property's name, category, or default, or you want to know whether a value is safe
to type by hand or gets overwritten the next time you sync.

## UCrowdySDKDeveloperSettings

The **Written by** column tells you which: **Config Sync** properties are read-only in Project Settings and
come from [Config Sync](../studio/config-sync.md); **you** properties are yours to edit directly.
`Environment` is an `ECrowdyEnvironment`: **Dev (shared)**, **Test**, **Production**, or **Custom**, which is
when the Discovery URL is read. Dev, Test, and Production each resolve to a built-in host
(`ck.dev.crowdedkingdoms.com`, `ck.test.crowdedkingdoms.com`, `ck.prod.crowdedkingdoms.com`); Custom is the
only value that reads `DiscoveryUrl` from the project. **Choose Production.** Dev and Test are Crowded
Kingdoms' internal environments: only staff and approved partners can sign in there, and any other account
is refused with `TIER_ACCESS_REQUIRED`.

<SurfaceTable table="settings" filter="class=UCrowdySDKDeveloperSettings" group="category" />

:::danger[Never hand-type a Config Sync property.]
The Network category is read-only in the editor on purpose, so Crowdy Studio stays the single source of
truth. A value pasted into the ini by hand is overwritten by the next sync, and a project whose settings
drift from its app fails to connect with no obvious error.
:::

:::warning[`UDPTimeoutSeconds` must stay above the SDK's ping interval.]
It is set on Crowdy Studio's Project page (Connection) and clamped to 6 to 120 seconds; the ping interval
is 5 seconds, so the floor already keeps it above. Too low and the SDK would re-assign a server during
normal traffic instead of only after a real drop.
:::

:::warning[`bAutoClearPersistentStateOnShutdown` fires only while UDP is still connected.]
It is not guaranteed at shutdown. For cleanup you can rely on, call `ClearAllState` before logout instead.
:::

:::info[`bShowConsentPrompt` is on by default.]
It opens the built-in terms and age prompt when a sign-in needs the player's agreement. Turn it off only if your game draws its own; see [Draw your own prompt](../services/authentication.md#draw-your-own-prompt).
:::

:::caution[Map profiles decide what the SDK does on each level.]
These settings point the SDK at an app; `MapProfiles` and `DefaultProfile` decide what it does per map. A
map with neither runs on the SDK's shipped default profile; a row whose asset does not load leaves the map
inactive. See [Map profile](../runtime/map-profile.md).
:::

`IDOverrides` and `ClassIDOverrides` exist only to resolve a startup type-id hash collision. Leave both
empty until the log reports one; in practice they stay empty for almost every project. A row is the type
and the id to force: an `FCrowdyIDOverride` holds `Struct` and `Override ID` (0 to 65535) for
`IDOverrides`; an `FCrowdyClassIDOverride` holds `Entity Class` and `Override ID` (1 or more) for
`ClassIDOverrides`.

### The default Backend

A project that has never run Config Sync's Backend selector has no `Environment` written to its
`DefaultGame.ini` yet, so it runs on whatever this SDK build defaults to: the tier the build was released
for. A build off the `dev` branch defaults to Dev, a `test` build to Test (both internal), and the public
release defaults to Production; the Discovery URL default follows the same tier. Read the active default from code with the
static `UCrowdySDKDeveloperSettings::GetReleaseEnvironment()` (C++ only, not exposed to Blueprint). Once you
pick a Backend on the Sign In page and sync, `DefaultGame.ini` holds that choice from then on and this
default no longer applies.

### Setting endpoints at runtime

Two runtime setters on `UCrowdySDKSubsystem` look like a way to configure these values in code, but they
are session-only overrides, not writes to the settings class: `SetDiscoveryUrl` stores a shared origin for
the current session and is only read when `Environment` is Custom, and `SetGameApiUrl` stores one Game API
HTTP endpoint for the session. `ReloadEndpointsFromSettings` is kept for old call sites and does nothing;
the API client already re-reads both endpoints from the settings on every call.

### Server Object gateway domains

A Server Object connects to the gateway the Game API names. The SDK connects only when that gateway is on the Game API's own domains, so a Game API that points somewhere else cannot receive the player's connect token. If you host the server yourself on a domain of your own, list it under **Project Settings, Crowdy SDK, Server Objects, Allowed Exec Gateway Domains** (`AllowedExecGatewayDomains` in `Config/DefaultGame.ini`, with the other Crowdy SDK settings). An entry such as `example.com` allows that domain and its subdomains. A scheme, a path, a port, a leading dot or `*.` in an entry is ignored, so `https://*.example.com:8443/` counts as `example.com`. An entry that does not read as a domain at all, such as `https://` or `*.`, allows nothing, and the SDK logs a Warning naming it when it checks a gateway outside the Game API's own domains.

A gateway outside both the Game API's own domains and this list is refused for good: every Server Object fails with a reason that starts "Could not open the connection to the server: the Game API named a gateway outside its own domains", and none is retried until you acquire it again (or call Restart). See [Troubleshooting](../exec/troubleshooting.md#what-makes-it-fail).

### Server Object timeouts

Two properties under **Crowdy SDK, Developer, Server Objects** set how long a Server Object connection waits. Like the Network category they are read-only in Project Settings and are edited on Crowdy Studio's Project page, in the **Connection** tab under **Server Objects**; see [Config Sync](../studio/config-sync.md).

- `ServerObjectCallTimeoutSeconds` (**Server Object Call Timeout**) is how long a call waits for the platform's answer before it fails with a `Timeout`: 11 to 120 seconds, 20 by default. It stays above the longest **Time per Call** a type may have, 10 seconds. A **Call** node's **Timeout** can shorten it for one call; see [Give up sooner](../exec/from-blueprint/call-functions.md#give-up-sooner).
- `ServerObjectOpenTimeoutSeconds` (**Server Object Open Timeout**) is how long opening the connection waits before the attempt fails: 1 to 60 seconds, 10 by default.

Both apply from the next Play, and to the editor's developer connections. A dropped connection is always reopened; there is no setting for that.

## Gotchas

- The class is `Config=Game`. A property you change in code at runtime through the settings object itself
  does not persist past the session; use the two runtime setters above for a session-only override instead.
- `MapProfiles` and `DefaultProfile` decide what runs per level; a property here being set correctly does
  not mean a given map resolved the profile you meant.
- The baked registry asset is required in a packaged build, but the `BakedRegistry` setting may stay empty:
  the SDK falls back to the fixed path the cook writes. See [Packaging](../guides/packaging.md).

## Related

- [Config Sync](../studio/config-sync.md): the authoring source for the Network category split.
- [Map profile](../runtime/map-profile.md): the other half of "make replication work".
- [Console variables](./console-cvars.md): the CVar surface alongside these settings.

# RPC Metadata Keys
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/reference/rpc-meta-keys

# RPC Metadata Keys

This page lists the metadata you place on a CrowdyEvent receiver to control routing and, for a Blueprint
custom event, to mark it as RPC-style in the first place.

Come here when you are writing or reviewing a `CrowdyEvent` receiver and need the exact key names, their
accepted values and defaults, and where each one is legal to place.

In C++ the keys go on the `UFUNCTION(meta=(...))` line of your `_Implementation` function.

```cpp
UFUNCTION(meta = (CrowdyEvent,
    CrowdyRecipient = "SpatialMulticast",
    CrowdyDecay = "Exponential_Decay",
    CrowdyDistance = "Four_Chunks"))
void FireWeapon_Implementation(int32 Ammo, FVector Direction);
CROWDY_EVENT(FireWeapon)
```

## Keys

The marker that turns a function into a CrowdyEvent receiver:

<SurfaceTable table="meta-keys" filter="key=CrowdyEvent" columns={["key", "symbol", "header"]} />

The routing keys that go alongside it, and the Blueprint-only markers that identify an RPC-style event to
the compiler:

<SurfaceTable table="meta-keys" filter="owner=CrowdyRpcMetaKeys" columns={["key", "symbol", "header"]} />

The manifest carries the symbol and its header; the accepted values, defaults, and behavior below come from
reading the header directly, since the manifest has no default or notes field for a meta key.

`CrowdyEvent` takes no value and is required on every receiver. Its legal place is any `UFUNCTION`, whether
you wrote the C++ by hand or the compiler generated it from a Blueprint custom event marked
`CrowdyReplicates`. Both a C++ receiver and a generated Blueprint one carry `CrowdyEvent`; only the
Blueprint one also needs `CrowdyReplicates` sitting next to it, because a Blueprint graph has no other way to
tell the router this custom event is RPC-style rather than a struct handler.

`CrowdyRecipient` takes an `ECrowdyEventRecipient` name and defaults to `SpatialMulticast`. The enumerators,
in declared order, are `SpatialMulticast`, `Multicast`, `OwningClient`, and `Host`. See
[enums](/unreal-sdk/reference/enums) for the full type.

`CrowdyDecay` takes an `ECrowdyDecayRate` name and defaults to `No_Decay`. The enumerators are `No_Decay`,
`Exponential_Decay`, `Linear_50`, `Linear_25`, `Linear_10`, and `Linear_5`. It applies only to
`SpatialMulticast`; the SDK reads it unconditionally, but it only changes anything on the spatial send path.

`CrowdyDistance` takes an `ECrowdyReplicationDistance` name and defaults to `Eight_Chunks`, the maximum
range. It applies only to `SpatialMulticast`, same as `CrowdyDecay`.

`CrowdyChannel` takes a channel name string and defaults to empty, which means the app-wide default session
channel. It names the channel a `Multicast` event routes over by name rather than id, so the same event
resolves to the same channel in every environment your app is deployed to.

`CrowdyAction` takes no value. It declares that the receiver's parameters describe a one-shot action, an
attack swing, a flinch, an emote, rather than a body to run. The Crowdy Mass Rendering Backend plays it as an
animation action on a receiver that holds the entity as a crowd row rather than a live actor. On the
actor pool the declaration changes nothing. See
[Play poses and one-shot actions](../mass/play-poses-and-one-shot-actions.md).

`CrowdyReplicates` takes no value. It marks a Blueprint custom event as RPC-style ("Crowdy Replicates" in
the Blueprint dropdown), which is what tells the router to bind it through the RPC path rather than as a
struct handler, and lets the compiler inject the dispatch gate. A C++ receiver never sets this key;
`CROWDY_EVENT` is the C++ equivalent.

`CrowdyReplicate` is a legacy alias of `CrowdyReplicates`, kept so an older Blueprint asset still resolves.
It is deliberately not reused by Crowdy State: the same string already means "this is an RPC event," so a
state property never carries it. See [state metadata keys](./state-meta-keys.md).

:::caution[The receiver must be a real `UFUNCTION`. The `CROWDY_EVENT(Name)` macro only generates the call
site. It cannot emit the `UFUNCTION`, because UnrealHeaderTool does not expand macros when it scans for
reflected functions.]
:::

:::warning[`CrowdyRecipient = "Host"` addresses the elected host. Election is a convention, not an
enforcement boundary, so do not treat Host-only delivery as a security control.]
Anyone can hold the host role at some point in a session. If a call must only take effect for a
server-validated reason, check that reason on the receiving end; do not rely on the recipient filter alone
to keep an untrusted client from reaching the logic.
:::

## Gotchas

- `CrowdyDecay` and `CrowdyDistance` are read unconditionally, but neither changes anything outside the
  `SpatialMulticast` recipient.
- `CrowdyReplicates` and its legacy alias `CrowdyReplicate` only ever appear on a Blueprint custom event; a
  C++ receiver never sets them.
- `CrowdyAction` is a declaration only. The actor pool ignores it; the Crowdy Mass Rendering Backend reads
  it to play the call as an action on a crowd row. See
  [Play poses and one-shot actions](../mass/play-poses-and-one-shot-actions.md).

## Related

- [State metadata keys](./state-meta-keys.md)
- [RPC parameter types](./rpc-types.md)
- [RPC Events in C++](/unreal-sdk/runtime/rpc-events-cpp)
- [Enums](./enums.md)

# Crowdy State Metadata Keys
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/reference/state-meta-keys

# Crowdy State Metadata Keys

This page lists the metadata you place on a property to control Crowdy State property replication. For the
full guide, see [Crowdy State](/unreal-sdk/runtime/crowdy-state).

Come here for the exact key names, their accepted values and defaults, and what a Crowdy State property may
hold.

In C++ the keys go on the `UPROPERTY(meta=(...))` line. In Blueprint they are set from the variable's
Details panel through the **Crowdy Replication** dropdown, not typed by hand.

```cpp
UPROPERTY(meta = (CrowdyState,
    CrowdyOnRep = "OnRep_Stance",
    CrowdyOwnerOnly,
    CrowdyManualDirty,
    CrowdyHeartbeat))
uint8 Stance = 0;

UFUNCTION()
void OnRep_Stance();
```

## Keys

<SurfaceTable table="meta-keys" filter="owner=CrowdyStateMetaKeys" columns={["key", "symbol", "header"]} />

The manifest carries the symbol and its header; the accepted values, defaults, and behavior below come from
the header directly.

`CrowdyState` takes no value and is required. It marks the property for Crowdy State; the other four keys
do nothing without it. Its legal place is any `UPROPERTY`, never a `UFUNCTION` or `UCLASS`.

`CrowdyOnRep` takes the name of a parameterless notify function and has no default. It runs on the receiver
right after the value is written, and only when the value actually changed: GAS-style, no arguments, no
previous value. Read the new value off the property itself.

`CrowdyOwnerOnly` takes no value and defaults to off. It is a delivery scope, not secrecy: the property
ships only to the entity's owning client, over the targeted single-actor path, never on the spatial
broadcast. This changes who receives the value, not who could intercept it.

`CrowdyManualDirty` takes no value and defaults to off. It skips the automatic per-tick diff; the value
ships only when you call `MarkStateDirty`. One mark sends exactly the next update, then clears. It is meant
for a big or expensive property you do not want diffed every tick.

`CrowdyHeartbeat` takes no value and defaults to off in C++. It opts a property into the periodic keyframe
baseline, so a late-relevant peer gets its current value. On-change replication is unaffected either way: a
changed property always ships, marked or not, marked properties are simply re-sent while unchanged too. The
Blueprint "Crowdy Replication" dropdown pre-checks Heartbeat the first time a variable enters Replicated
mode, as a convenience; the underlying mechanism is the same opt-in metadata either way.

:::note[`CrowdyOwnerOnly`, `CrowdyManualDirty`, and `CrowdyHeartbeat` are presence markers. You add the bare key to turn each on; they take no value. The code tests only whether the key is present, so do not write `= true` -- and `= false` would still count as on. `CrowdyOnRep` is the one key that takes a value, the notify function's name.]
:::

:::note[`CrowdyState` is deliberately not spelled `CrowdyReplicate`. That string already belongs to the RPC side, as an alias of the Blueprint marker `CrowdyReplicates`. Reusing it here would make one key mean two different systems and break RPC-versus-state discovery. If you came from the RPC metadata keys page expecting the two families to mirror each other by name, they do not, on purpose. See [RPC metadata keys](./rpc-meta-keys.md).]
:::

## What can be marked

Crowdy State covers plain values and plain structs: numbers, bools, enums, `FName`, `FString`, and USTRUCTs built from those. Object references, containers (`TArray`, `TSet`, `TMap`, including buried inside a struct), and static arrays are rejected at discovery and simply do not replicate. See [Unsupported types](/unreal-sdk/runtime/crowdy-state#rejected) for the full list and the reasons.

A struct type that carries a native net serializer (`FVector_NetQuantize`, `FRotator`, and the rest of the `_NetQuantize` family) quantizes on the wire automatically, with no key to set. See [type-driven quantization](/unreal-sdk/runtime/crowdy-state#accepted).

The Blueprint "Crowdy Replication" dropdown offers **None** and **Replicated**; **Replicated** writes these keys for you. A `CrowdyModel` or `CrowdyContainer` key left on a property from the removed Game Model API does nothing; see [Move from Game Models](../exec/move-from-game-models.md#upgrade-steps).

:::warning[`HasMetaData`-backed discovery helpers, including the one behind this header, answer false in a cooked build, because cooked builds strip metadata. A runtime check routes through the baked registry instead, never through live metadata.]
:::

## Gotchas

- All five keys go on a `UPROPERTY`; none apply to a `UFUNCTION` or `UCLASS`.
- `CrowdyHeartbeat` only changes how often an unchanged value is re-sent. A changed value always ships,
  heartbeat or not.
- A property is discovered live only in the editor. A packaged build reads the baked rep table, not the
  metadata on the header.

## Related

- [Crowdy State](/unreal-sdk/runtime/crowdy-state): owner diffing, host precedence, world entities, and the
  keyframe baseline.
- [RPC metadata keys](./rpc-meta-keys.md)

# Enums
Source: https://docs.crowdedkingdoms.com/unreal-sdk/reference/enums

# Enums

The enums you reach for most often when working with entities, RPC events, and Crowdy State properties, described in full below. Every other BlueprintType enum the SDK exposes is in the generated table at the end of this page, so a name you cannot find in the ten sections here is still worth a search there before you open a header.

## ECrowdyEventRecipient

Who runs a CrowdyEvent, and over which transport.

Header: `Core/UDP/Enums/ECrowdyMessageType.h`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `SpatialMulticast` | Everyone in range runs it, over the spatial path, thinned by decay and distance. The default. |
| `Multicast` | Every member of the session channel runs it, over the channel transport, at any distance with no decay. |
| `OwningClient` | Only the client that owns the target entity runs it. |
| `Host` | Only the elected host runs it. The host may act on any entity it has locally. |

:::note[`SpatialMulticast` is the default recipient. For a full walkthrough of how each value selects its transport, see [Recipients and Routing](/unreal-sdk/runtime/recipients-and-routing).]
:::

## ECrowdyDecayRate

How delivery probability falls off with distance.

:::tip[Decay applies only to `SpatialMulticast`. It has no effect on the other recipients.]
:::

| Value |
| --- |
| `No_Decay` |
| `Exponential_Decay` |
| `Linear_50` |
| `Linear_25` |
| `Linear_10` |
| `Linear_5` |

## ECrowdyReplicationDistance

The maximum distance, in chunks, that a `SpatialMulticast` event travels from the sender.

Values: `None`, `One_Chunk`, `Two_Chunks`, `Three_Chunks`, `Four_Chunks`, `Five_Chunks`, `Six_Chunks`, `Seven_Chunks`, `Eight_Chunks`.

`Eight_Chunks` is the default.

## ECrowdyEntityMode

How an entity replicates. Set it on `UCrowdyEntityComponent`.

Header: `Replication/Components/CrowdyEntityComponent.h`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Dynamic` | The continuous state channel streams the executor's snapshot every interval. Use it for movement and anything high frequency. |
| `Static` | Event only. State travels through `SendEvent` and CrowdyEvent handlers. |

## ECrowdyIdentityPolicy

How an entity gets its `NetID`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PlayerDerived` | From the signed in user id. Only valid on the locally controlled player pawn. |
| `Stable` | Hashed from the actor's level path. Every client computes the same id for a level placed actor. |
| `Random` | A fresh id each session. Use for runtime spawns. |

## ECrowdyRole

This client's relationship to an entity.

Header: `Data/CrowdyEntityTypes.h`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | Not registered. |
| `Owner` | This client simulates the entity and sends its state and events. |
| `RemoteProxy` | This client receives state and events from the network. |
| `HostOwned` | Owned by whoever is host. Reassigned on host migration. |

## ECrowdyOwnership

The authority axis for an entity: who owns and simulates it. Set it on `UCrowdyEntityComponent`. It is orthogonal to `ECrowdyEntityMode` and `ECrowdyIdentityPolicy`, and mostly matters for level placed world entities (a runtime host spawn is already owner on the host).

Header: `Replication/Components/CrowdyEntityComponent.h`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `LocalClient` | This client owns and simulates the entity (`Role=Owner`). The default. |
| `Host` | Owned by whichever client is currently host (`Role=HostOwned`, no per client owner). Use it for world or AI entities that must share one authority across every client. |

## ECrowdyHostOverride

Whether the elected host may super-user-write a client owned entity's Crowdy State. Set it on `UCrowdyEntityComponent`. Only meaningful when `Ownership` is `LocalClient`.

Header: `Replication/Components/CrowdyEntityComponent.h`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Allow` | The host may override this entity's Crowdy State as a super-user, and the owner adopts the correction. The default. |
| `OwnerOnly` | Only the owning client may change this entity. Even a host-sourced correction is dropped. |

:::note[Host authority on the Crowdy State plane is a precedence-by-convention, not a server-enforced boundary. Keep authoritative or cheat-sensitive state off this plane. See [host authority](/unreal-sdk/runtime/host-authority).]
:::

## ECrowdyStateHeartbeat

Per entity control over the Crowdy State keyframe heartbeat, the periodic re-send of `CrowdyHeartbeat`-marked properties. Set it on `UCrowdyEntityComponent`. On-change replication is unaffected either way.

Header: `Replication/Components/CrowdyEntityComponent.h`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Inherit` | Follow the map profile. Marked properties re-send every `StateKeyframeIntervalSeconds` when the map's keyframe interval is greater than 0. The default. |
| `Off` | Never emit a keyframe heartbeat for this entity, regardless of its property marks or the map setting. A kill switch for always-active entities. |

## ECrowdyReplicationMode

The mode chosen in the "Crowdy Replication" dropdown on a Blueprint variable's Details panel. Editor only.

Header: `Customizations/CrowdyReplicationMode.h`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | Not networked by Crowdy. Selecting it scrubs every Crowdy key off the variable. |
| `Replicated` | Crowdy State: the fast, client-authoritative view plane. Stamps the Crowdy State metadata so the variable flows through the same discovery and bake as a C++ `meta=(CrowdyState)` property. |

:::note[For how to author a replicated variable, see [Crowdy State](/unreal-sdk/runtime/crowdy-state).]
:::

## Every BlueprintType enum

The ten above are the ones this page explains in prose. The table below is generated from the same manifest that backs the rest of this reference section, grouped by module, and it lists every BlueprintType enum the manifest reports, including ones no page describes in words. Two wire-level enums no Blueprint-callable takes, `ECrowdyMessageType` and `ECrowdyErrorCode`, are BlueprintType in the header but missing from the manifest's enum group in this export, so they are absent below. The manifest carries each enum's name, its enumerator list, and where it lives, but not a meaning for each value, so for the "why" behind a value you still want the sections above or the concept page a row links to.

<SurfaceTable table="enums" group="module" />

Thirteen enums the manifest reports are excluded from the table above: two are deprecated (the persistence pull result and the connection monitor's reconnect state), one is a transport protocol enumeration nothing game-facing selects, and ten belong to another first-party module that rides in the same plugin build and are outside this SDK's own contract. None of them is part of the surface a game calls.

## Gotchas

- The generated table's page column is blank where no other page mentions the enum by name; that is a gap in the docs, not a sign the enum does not exist.
- A value's meaning lives in the ten prose sections above or on the concept page it links to, never in the generated table, which only has names.
